Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after his affair raises national security concerns
|                            Getting your Trinity Audio player ready...                        | 
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after his extramarital affair raised national security concerns, in a spectacular downfall for the longtime head of the chipmaker, a vital player in the artificial intelligence boom.
The company named Colette Kress as interim chief executive. She is the current executive vice president and chief financial officer.
Huang faced growing calls to resign after his affair with a Chinese businesswoman who reportedly was also acting as a spy for Beijing. His troubles compounded late Wednesday after media reports said Huang had another extramarital affair with an Nvidia employee who reported to him.
Kress took over the role as Nvidia’s chief financial officer in 2013, overseeing the company’s global finance operations. Before that, she worked for three years at Cisco and spent 13 years at Microsoft.
In a statement Thursday, Kress said that Nvidia’s “strength has always come from its people” and that she was “committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years.”
The board of directors said Thursday it had also named its first-ever chairman, Harvey C. Jones, an entrepreneur and venture investor.
Shares of Nvidia tumbled 14% at the opening bell Thursday, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq slid 1.5%
Nvidia’s board had gathered to discuss Huang’s future after revelations about his affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed International suspected of being a Chinese government agent. The two are not related.
In its first statement since the scandal broke, Megaspeed said Thursday that it takes its obligation to comply with U.S. export control laws “extremely seriously.” The company prominently touts a partnership with Nvidia on its website. The two are not related.
Details about Huang’s affair with the former Megaspeed executive are unclear.
“Megaspeed is committed to working constructively and transparently with the U.S. government,” said the statement signed by its chairman and CEO, Tan Yong Pong, who also goes by James Tan.
Nvidia has said it had “no reason to believe” that either national security or its secrets were compromised, but that its inquiry would examine all available information.
Last month, the Times reported that U.S. intelligence agencies discovered that Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang — and determined that she was feeding information directly to Beijing. On Sunday, U.S. President Donald Trump announced that the FBI was investigating.
Megaspeed faced allegations last year that it was illicitly shipping advanced Nvidia computer chips into China, but in December said there was “no evidence” of such exports.
Singaporean authorities said Thursday that they questioned Alice Huang and confiscated her passport last year as part of an investigation into Megaspeed. They concluded last year that there wasn’t enough evidence that she had committed a crime but barred her from returning to the country.
China has denied that it engaged in an attempt to ensnare Huang, who heads one of the world’s most valuable companies. Nvidia has become a leader in making chips that power AI and Huang has lobbied Washington to loosen limits on sales of Nvidia chips to China. In January, he won Trump’s approval to sell its H200 chips to China.
Megaspeed said Thursday that it has cooperated with the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), which handles enforcement of national security restrictions on technology exports, and was ready to “cooperate fully with any other relevant U.S. government authority.”

sources.news_title: The Downfall of Jensen Huang and What’s Next for Nvidia
sources.text:
Less than two weeks ago, billionaire Jensen Huang was a gainfully employed CEO whose personal life the general public knew very little about; today, he’s out at Nvidia, the multitrillion-dollar company he co-founded in 1993, following revelations that he had an affair with (1) a woman accused of being a Chinese spy and (2) an Nvidia subordinate.
On Wednesday Nvidia’s board met for hours to decide Huang’s fate, and, despite the CEO reportedly “fighting hard to hang onto his role with the company he founded,” Huang resigned Thursday morning and chief financial officer Colette Kress was appointed interim CEO. Incredibly, Nvidia had no successor in place prior to the scandal that took down its leader because Huang didn’t believe in succession planning; he was also apparently a micromanager with 60 direct reports and said last year that he reads thousands of employee emails a day. According to The Information, Huang told colleagues in the past several years that he would run Nvidia until he is 120 years old. Which is all well and good if you’re planning to both (a) live that long and (b) not have an affair with an accused Chinese spy. Otherwise it’s pretty risky!
The stunning downfall will undoubtedly have reverberations far beyond Nvidia’s Silicon Valley campus, given Huang’s position as one of the most powerful, if not the most powerful, figures in the AI industry and his close proximity to Donald Trump. On Wall Street, the company’s stock was down 11 percent on the news of his departure, which translates to a loss of roughly $1 trillion just this month. In Washington, the New York Times notes that few tech executives “have had as much sway as Huang over Trump’s approach to A.I. and China.” He reportedly “persuaded the president to roll back a ban on chip sales to China and Nvidia has donated at least $20 million to a fund for Trump’s White House ballroom project.”
On Thursday morning, Trump — who spent the prior days telling reporters how wonderful Huang is — recommended former Apple CEO Tim Cook for the job. Trump has gushed in the past about “Tim Apple,” who visited the White House last year bearing gifts. “A Legend replaces a Legend!” the president wrote.
If you’re just catching up to the sex-spy-AI scandal, here’s everything that’s happened so far.
  
  
    .
October 29: The Times reports Huang had a “close relationship” with a suspected spy
    
In a bombshell story, the New York Times reports that after concluding that Alice Huang (no relation), the chief executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed, was a “Chinese intelligence asset,” U.S. intelligence officials made an even more startling discovery: that Huang “had developed a close relationship with Jensen Huang.” The Times story also reveals that Donald Trump had been “briefed about the intelligence findings” a year ago and “chose not to do anything with the information.” In fairness, the president may have been preoccupied with ballroom renovations; at the time, he was fighting with his architect.
  
  
    .
Later on October 29: Huang says there’s nothing to see here
    
In an interview with Bloomberg, the CEO insists his interactions with Ms. Huang were strictly professional. “Our relationship, our interactions, have been related to Megaspeed, and it was all completely normal and not unusual,” Huang says. He will regret this statement!
  
  
    .
November 5: Republicans ask Huang to sit for closed-door interview
    
GOP representatives Brian Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford — who lead the House’s Committee on Foreign Affairs, the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, and the Select Committee on Intelligence, respectively — send a letter to Huang telling him they want a closed-door briefing on his interactions with Ms. Huang. “Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information,” they write. “The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress. It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk.”
  
  
    .
November 7: The likely new head of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee demands answers
    
Democratic senator Chris Coons, who is expected to chair the Senate Foreign Relations Committee come January, writes on X: “The more I learn about the insane relationship between the Trump Administration, Chinese spies, and AI billionaires, the more I’m convinced there is nothing this administration does that isn’t corrupt. Congress will investigate and get answers.”
  
  
    .
November 8: Huang admits to the affair, says company is opening an investigation
    
In a letter to Nvidia employees, Huang — who denied the affair less than two weeks prior — writes: “I owe my family and all of you an apology. I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” He continues: “Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, NVIDIA’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American.” In a statement, Nvidia’s board says it “has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team.”
  
  
    .
Later on November 8: Trump defends Huang like a brother, repeatedly declares how awesome the guy is
    
Speaking to reporters the day Huang admitted to the affair, Trump says he would “certainly take” the CEO on an upcoming trip to China and that Huang “dealt with somebody, but you know, so does everybody else.” (As a reminder, the president himself is an expert on affairs.) The president of the United States continues: “I think he’s an honorable guy. I think he probably has an excuse for it. You have to hear it … He’s done an amazing job for our country. You know, we have the hottest country anywhere in the world. We have the highest stock market.”
  
  
    .
Also on November 8: The Times reports Marco Rubio circulated a big, flashing warning about Huang to administration officials
    
The Times runs a story reporting that last year, the secretary of State “oversaw the drafting” of a “highly classified memo” that warned top officials in the Trump administration that Huang “was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy.” The memo was reportedly sent to officials prior to a trip the president took to China in May; according to the Times, it’s unclear if the warning played a role in Huang initially not being invited to join Trump. (After Trump saw coverage about Huang not being included on the delegation, he wrote on social media that he was honored to have “the Great Jensen Huang” and other business executives “journeying to the Great Country of China where I will be asking President Xi, a Leader of extraordinary distinction, to ‘open up’ China so that these brilliant people can work their magic.” (Huang was picked up by Air Force One during a stop in Alaska.)
  
  
    .
November 9: Trump tells reporters Huang is “suffering,” says he heard about the affair “not too long ago”
    
In fact, he was told about it a year ago and chose not to do anything.
  
  
    .
Also on November 9: Report reveals that Commerce Department’s Nvidia investigation was abruptly halted
    
The Times reports that a “monthslong investigation” into Megaspeed, and whether it was “smuggling Nvidia’s artificial intelligence chips into China,” was suddenly paused “after Commerce Department investigators working on the case received an email from Nvidia’s general counsel seeking information about the inquiry.” Agents were reportedly alarmed when Nvidia’s general counsel said that a top Commerce official who reports directly to Secretary Howard Lutnick “had given Nvidia permission to reach out about the case.”
  
  
    .
November 10: Nvidia retains Wachtell to investigate
    
The board of directors announces it has hired Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to run the investigation into Huang’s affair and whether company secrets were divulged or national security was breached. The probe will be run by Joon Kim, the former acting U.S. Attorney for the Southern District who was appointed in 2021 to investigate allegations of sexual harassment against then-governor Andrew Cuomo.
  
  
    .
November 11: Oops, Huang had another affair
    
As it turns out, the Nvidia CEO wasn’t just having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, he was also cheating on his wife with a subordinate named Kimberly Powell, according to the New York Times. And apparently he’d been hoping to keep that affair on the down low. Per the Times:
In March, Ms. Powell appeared at GTC, Nvidia’s annual developer conference in San Jose, where she spoke about using A.I. to aid in breakthroughs in health care and biology. Her presentation used cartoon depictions of Mr. Huang.
During the conference, Nvidia executives were at a nearby hotel for meetings. Mr. Huang and Ms. Powell were seen being affectionate at the hotel. One bystander captured the interaction on their phone, three people briefed on the incident said.
Mr. Huang’s security workers witnessed the bystander with the phone and sequestered the person, the people said. The workers then asked the person to sign a nondisclosure agreement.
When asked by a reporter about the relationship by phone, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” and hung up.
  
  
    .
Later on November 11: Nvidia’s board meets to discuss Huang, whose job security doesn’t appear super-solid
    
The Wall Street Journal reports that Nvidia’s board of directors “is preparing to oust” Huang. Of note, there is no successor in place.
  
  
    .
November 12: Nvidia’s board announces Huang has resigned
    
After meeting for hours on Wednesday, Nvidia announces early Thursday morning that Huang has resigned, despite reportedly “fighting hard to hang onto his role.” Chief finance officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO with the search for a permanent replacement starting immediately. The board also says it has appointed its first-ever chairman, Harvey Jones, the former CEO of Synopsys.

sources.news_title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang, AI godfather brought down by spy scandal
sources.text:
Nvidia's Jensen Huang, AI godfather brought down by spy scandal
New York (AFP) – Chips designed by Nvidia push the boundaries of artificial intelligence, and its leather-jacket-wearing leader Jensen Huang built the company into one of the world's most important brands over his 33 years at the helm.
Issued on: Modified:
Unknown to the public just four years ago, the 63-year-old recently emerged as a powerful public entrepreneur, drawing stadium crowds as he presented cutting-edge components essential to the development of AI tools like ChatGPT.
But Huang was forced out of the company that he co-founded when a scandal exploded over his personal life, as he admitted to having an affair with a woman whom US officials believe was working for Chinese intelligence.
Huang resigned as chief executive on Thursday and also gave up his seat on the board. The company did not give a reason for his departure.
Nvidia earlier opened a probe into Huang, who acknowledged having been unfaithful to his wife and said he was "deeply sorry."
Huang reportedly had an affair with Alice Huang -- who is of no relation -- a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed.
The New York Times had reported Wednesday that Huang was involved in a second extramarital affair with a subordinate.
Tough early life
Big tech's insatiable appetite for chips designed by Nvidia, known as Graphics Processing Units (GPUs), has catapulted the California chip designer to a market valuation of $4.5 trillion, among the world's largest.
Its meteoric rise made Huang one of the world's richest people -- worth around $160 billion, according to Forbes -- thanks to the roughly four percent stake he holds in the company he founded three decades ago with two friends in a Silicon Valley diner.
He has become a close informal adviser on AI to Donald Trump, traveling with the US president on Air Force One to Beijing earlier this year.
That is an area of concern to US officials who believe he has been involved with the alleged spy, Alice Huang.
Born in Taipei in 1963, Jensen Huang -- originally named Jen-Hsun -- embodies the American success story.
At nine years old, he was sent away with his brother to boarding school in small-town Kentucky.
His uncle recommended the school to his Taiwanese parents believing it to be a prestigious institution, though it was actually a school for troubled youth.
Too young to be a student, Huang boarded there but attended a nearby public school alongside the children of tobacco farmers. With his poor English, he was bullied and forced to clean toilets -- a two-year ordeal that transformed him.
"We worked really hard, we studied really hard, and the kids were really tough," he recounted in an interview with US broadcaster NPR. But "the ending of the story is I loved the time I was there."
Brought home by his parents who had by then settled in the northwestern US state of Oregon, he graduated from university at just 20 and joined AMD, then LSI Logic, to design chips -- his passion.
Megastar in Taiwan
He wanted to go further and founded Nvidia in 1993 to "solve problems that normal computers can't," using semiconductors powerful enough to handle 3D graphics, he said during an interview on the "No Priors" podcast.
Nvidia created the first GPU in 1999, riding the intersection of video games, data centers, cloud computing and now generative AI.
Always dressed in a black T-shirt and leather jacket, Huang sports a Nvidia logo tattoo and has a taste for sports cars.
One former high-ranking Nvidia employee described him to AFP as "the most driven person" he'd ever met.
He has rejected calls to deliberately slow down AI development even as some insiders warn the technology could threaten human existence within a decade.
"That kind of narrative is dramatic, it gets a lot of attention," but "it's not grounded on facts," he told CBS News in September.
"We should go as fast as we can" on AI, but labs should not release products that are not safe, he said.
On visits to his native Taiwan, Huang is received like a megastar, with fans crowding him for autographs and selfies as journalists follow him to the barber shop and his favorite night market.
Nvidia had taken care to project a drama-free image of Huang.
But the former employee described a "very paradoxical" individual protective of his employees but also capable, within Nvidia's executive circle, of "ripping people to shreds" over mistakes or poor decisions.
© 2026 AFP

sources.news_title: Global AI stocks sink as Nvidia CEO's exit deepens sector concerns
sources.text:
Global AI-linked stocks tumbled on Thursday as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned following a deepening scandal around his affairs, upending the chipmaker's leadership and posing fresh risks to a sector already reeling with funding and regulatory concerns.
Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor, the company said.
As the centerpiece of the AI ecosystem, the chipmaker finances infrastructure built around its chips - a strategy that has drawn scrutiny over circular funding and now risks weighing on the sector as its crisis deepens.
Nvidia's shares fell 8.2% to a more than 16-month low in early trading and its market value was on track to close below $4 trillion for the first time since July 2025.
"Nvidia has been called the 'Bank of AI'. If they have to take a step back because of what's going on, will that cut off funding to smaller companies that need it? That's an open question," said Joe Saluzzi, partner and co-head of equity trading at Themis Trading.
Nvidia-backed neocloud firms CoreWeave dropped 9.1% after surging more than 27% in the previous session when its earnings ignited a relief rally in AI stocks.
Other neocloud stocks including IREN and Applied Digital were also trading lower. Nebius dropped 16.2% after the company said its 2026 revenue would come in at the low end of its previous forecast.
Nvidia has lost more than $550 billion in market value since the board announced an investigation on Sunday into Huang's relationship with a businesswoman called Alice Huang, who is alleged to be a Chinese spy.
"The interlocking deals that Nvidia has with so much of the industry raises the question into whether that created more stability or more fragility. We're going to find out over the next few weeks as this whole situation unravels," said Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers.
Nvidia short sellers have made $9.6 billion in on paper profits so far this week, according to data analytics firm ORTEX.
AI SELLOFF CONTINUES AFTER BRIEF RESPITE
Chipmakers, widely viewed as one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom, led the selloff with the Philadelphia chips index sliding 1.3%.
Marvell Technology, which Huang called as the "next trillion dollar company" in June, slumped 3.8%. AI hyperscaler Oracle, which is expanding its cloud AI chip deals with Nvidia, shed 2.6%.
Memory chipmaker Micron Technology fell 2.5% and data storage firms Sandisk and Western Digital eased 6% and 3.7%. Photonic product makers Lumentum and Coherent and AI server maker Dell eased between 3% and 5.1%.
Construction and power-generation equipment maker Caterpillar and power producer Vistra slipped about 0.5% each.
Shares of AMD and Broadcom, which also produce AI chips and compete with Nvidia, however, rose 3.7% and 5.6%, respectively, on expectations that the turmoil at Nvidia could create opportunity for rivals.
Other hyperscalers including Alphabet, Amazon.com and Microsoft were also up between 0.8% and 2.7%.
AI stocks struggled and the Nasdaq entered a technical correction earlier this month after the Democrats swept the midterm elections, including in states opposed to data centers, stoking fears tighter regulation could slow the AI build-out.
Tech-heavy stock markets across the globe witnessed jitters. Japan and South Korea closed nearly 0.7% lower. Tech stocks in Europe were also down about 1%.
Nvidia trades at about 12 times its 12-month forward earnings estimates, its lowest since November 2012, according to data compiled by LSEG.

sources.news_title: Nvidia CEO resigns after spy affair – The Horn News
sources.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after his extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy raised national security concerns, in a spectacular downfall for the longtime head of the chipmaker, a vital player in the artificial intelligence boom.
The company named Colette Kress as interim chief executive. She is the current executive vice president and chief financial officer.
Huang faced growing calls to resign after his affair with a Chinese businesswoman who reportedly was also acting as a spy for Beijing. His troubles compounded late Wednesday after media reports said Huang had another extramarital affair with an Nvidia employee who reported to him.
Kress took over the role as Nvidia’s chief financial officer in 2013, overseeing the company’s global finance operations. Before that, she worked for three years at Cisco and spent 13 years at Microsoft.
In a statement Thursday, Kress said that Nvidia’s “strength has always come from its people” and that she was “committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years.”
The board of directors said Thursday it had also named its first-ever chairman, Harvey C. Jones, an entrepreneur and venture investor.
Shares of Nvidia tumbled 14% at the opening bell Thursday, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq slid 1.5%
Nvidia’s board had gathered to discuss Huang’s future after revelations about his affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed International suspected of being a Chinese government agent. The two are not related.
In its first statement since the scandal broke, Megaspeed said Thursday that it takes its obligation to comply with U.S. export control laws “extremely seriously.” The company prominently touts a partnership with Nvidia on its website. The two are not related.
Details about Huang’s affair with the former Megaspeed executive are unclear.
“Megaspeed is committed to working constructively and transparently with the U.S. government,” said the statement signed by its chairman and CEO, Tan Yong Pong, who also goes by James Tan.
Nvidia has said it had “no reason to believe” that either national security or its secrets were compromised, but that its inquiry would examine all available information.
Last month, the Times reported that U.S. intelligence agencies discovered that Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang — and determined that she was feeding information directly to Beijing. On Sunday, U.S. President Donald Trump announced that the FBI was investigating.
Megaspeed faced allegations last year that it was illicitly shipping advanced Nvidia computer chips into China, but in December said there was “no evidence” of such exports.
Singaporean authorities said Thursday that they questioned Alice Huang and confiscated her passport last year as part of an investigation into Megaspeed. They concluded last year that there wasn’t enough evidence that she had committed a crime but barred her from returning to the country.
China has denied that it engaged in an attempt to ensnare Huang, who heads one of the world’s most valuable companies. Nvidia has become a leader in making chips that power AI and Huang has lobbied Washington to loosen limits on sales of Nvidia chips to China. In January, he won Trump’s approval to sell its H200 chips to China.
Megaspeed said Thursday that it has cooperated with the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), which handles enforcement of national security restrictions on technology exports, and was ready to “cooperate fully with any other relevant U.S. government authority.”
It said it has hired a U.S. law firm to conduct a “comprehensive census” of its computer chips and to verify its export controls.
“Megaspeed welcomes appropriate government scrutiny and is committed to demonstrating through concrete actions that it operates responsibly, transparently, and in accordance with applicable U.S. laws,” it said.
Apart from questions over national security, Megaspeed’s finances also have drawn attention. Its total assets soared roughly 90-fold from late 2023 to 2024, to almost US$3 billion, according to Singapore corporate records.
Revenue surged to over US$294 million in 2024 from none in 2023.
The Associated Press contributed to this article

The company she worked for purchased chips from Nvidia and was investigated on suspicion of helping China obtain advanced chips subject to American export restrictions.
Nvidia's board of directors announced an independent investigation into allegations that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The company said at this time it has no reason to believe that its secrets or U.S. national security were compromised.
Following the board's announcement of Huang's resignation, the company's stock plunged more than 10 percent in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Since the affair was published, the company has lost more than $500 billion in its market value.

sources.text:
Huang has been in the eye of a storm after it was revealed that he had an affair with Alice Huang (not his relation) a Chinese businesswoman who it is claimed is an alleged Chinese Intel asset.
The aftermath of the alleged 'Chinese spy scandal' has hit Nvidia, with CEO Jensen Huang opting to resign amidst mounting pressure, reported Reuters.
Key Points
- Chief financial officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor, the company said.
- Huang has been in the eye of a storm after it was revealed that he had an affair with Alice Huang (not his relation) a Chinese businesswoman who it is claimed is an alleged Chinese Intel asset.
- Jensen Huang was also reported have had another affair with a senior executive of Nvidia Kimberly Powell.
Chief financial officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor, the company said on Thursday.
Huang has been in the eye of a storm after it was revealed that he had an affair with Alice Huang (not his relation) a Chinese businesswoman who it is claimed is an alleged Chinese Intel asset.
Jensen Huang was also reported have had another affair with a senior executive of Nvidia Kimberly Powell.
Jensen Huang had acknowledged his affair with Alice Huang in a letter to Nvidia employees where he apologised for being unfaithful to his wife and violating her trust.
Nvidia's board had also initiated an investigation into the matter, with the inquiry being led by law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz.
In May 2026 a Wall Street 'Short seller' Culper research had flagged Huang's alleged links to Alice Huang (the woman now claimed to be a Chinese Intel asset).
According to CBS News, on May 13 this year Culper Research published a 40-page report highlighting Huang's ties to Alice Huang, a former television reporter and financial industry executive.
According to the report, a copy of which is with ANI, Culper research said, "Nvidia has repeatedly vouched for Megaspeed – its single largest Southeast Asian chip buyer currently under investigation by both US Commerce and Singapore authorities."
"Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has not only vouched for Megaspeed, but seems to have quite literally walked alongside Megaspeed at every step, while maintaining an uncomfortably close relationship with Megaspeed’s Alice Huang, a Chinese national. He was first spotted partying with Alice Huang in June 2024 – the same month the Apex/Alibaba pledge was filed. He then dined with Alice Huang in Taiwan in May 2025 – just weeks after the news of U.S. trade restrictions. Finally, per one current Megaspeed employee, Jensen visits Megaspeed-linked data centers “every few months” and “every single time” he visits, he is accompanied by representatives from Alibaba. The Megaspeed employee characterized their relationship with Jensen as “very close”, corroborating another former Nvidia employee’s suggestion to us that many Nvidia employees wondered if there was a special relationship," the report stated.
Although Jensen Huang had got the backing of US President Donald Trump he was under extreme pressure with members of the US Congress flagging potential security risk of the affair with the alleged Chinese spy.
Jensen Huang's exit puts the $4 trillion Nvidia in troubled waters and could potentially disrupt the AI industry which has been facing headwinds on the markets recently.

sources.news_title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid Chinese espionage controversy; Colette Kress named interim chief
sources.text:
WASHINGTON DC: US tech gaint Nvidia’s co-founder Jensen Huang has resigned as president and chief executive with immediate effect, following a board meeting on 12 November amid mounting controversy over his personal relationships and allegations involving a Chinese businesswoman suspected of having links to CCP’s intelligence.
The tech company appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as Nvidia’s interim CEO. She will retain her existing positions as executive vice-president and CFO while overseeing the company until a permanent successor is appointed. Nvidia’s board has initiated a search for a new chief executive and will consider both internal and external candidates.
Huang, 63, co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and led its transformation into one of the world’s most valuable technology companies. His departure marks a significant leadership change at the chipmaker, which has become central to the global artificial intelligence industry.
The announcement triggered further selling in Nvidia shares, which fell approximately 10 per cent in US premarket trading. The decline added to a series of losses that had wiped out around $600 billion in the company’s market value during the week.
Personal controversy and Chinese espionage allegations
The leadership crisis followed reports concerning two extramarital relationships involving Huang. One involved Alice Huang, a businesswoman and former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, who was suspected by US intelligence officials of having connections to Chinese intelligence.
Reports alleged that her business network facilitated shipments of restricted Nvidia AI chips to Chinese companies. Nvidia’s board had commissioned an independent investigation into the matter, while the company previously maintained that it had no indication that its trade secrets or US national security had been compromised.
A separate report identified another alleged relationship involving Kimberly Powell, an Nvidia healthcare executive. Huang had acknowledged infidelity and apologised to his family and colleagues. US President Donald Trump had described CEO Huang as an “honorable guy”, while congressional leaders called for investigations into possible national security implications of the allegations.
Succession challenge at the chipmaking giant
Huang owned approximately 3.6 per cent of Nvidia’s shares and maintained dozens of direct reporting relationships, reflecting his central role in the company’s management. His departure raises questions about how the company will manage the transition after more than three decades under its co-founder.
Kress, who joined Nvidia in 2013, will lead the company on an interim basis while continuing her financial responsibilities. Senior executive Ian Buck, who oversees Nvidia’s data centre GPU business, has also featured in discussions about potential succession candidates.
The board’s search for a permanent chief executive will determine Nvidia’s leadership beyond the immediate transition.

sources.news_title: After days of controversy, Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang has resigned amid investigation and affair scandal
sources.text:
After days of controversy, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned
Hit the road Jacket.
Nvidia's founder and CEO Jensen Huang has resigned from his position as leader of one of the most valuable companies in the world.
After days mired in controversy, which began amid reports of Huang's alleged affair with a Chinese spy, Nvidia has announced Huang's resignation as company president, chief executive officer, and board member, effective immediately. Finance chief Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO and will remain in the position until a permanent CEO is chosen.
"Colette has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position," Harvey Jones, chair of Nvidia's board of directors wrote in a statement accompanying the news. "She is supported by an experienced leadership team that has been instrumental in executing Nvidia's strategy and advancing its technology roadmap. The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption."
Kress, in the same announcement, says she intends to build on the foundation laid by Huang over the past 33 years, and "continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead." Perhaps unsurprisingly, there's no mention of gaming graphics cards in there.
Nvidia's announcement ends by thanking Huang for his time at the company: "Jensen’s contributions to Nvidia are profound. Nvidia is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry."
Nvidia's board met on Wednesday to decide whether to remove Huang amid allegations he had participated in a second affair, this time with a subordinate, following reports of his alleged affair with a Chinese spy. That initial incident prompted a company-wide apology from Huang and an independent investigation exploring whether he'd been the target of a "foreign intelligence effort".
Nvidia will likely remain under increased scrutiny moving forward. There are particular concerns around the company's chips being imported to China despite trade bans.

sources.news_title: Nvidia stock falls following CEO resignation
sources.text:
Nvidia stocks fell sharply Thursday morning following news that founder and CEO Jensen Huang resigned following reports he was the target of a “foreign intelligence effort.”
The stock dropped 12.6% at opening Thursday, to $150.99.
The New York Times first reported Huang’s affair with a suspected Chinese spy last month. On Sunday, Nvidia’s board announced an investigation, and Huang issued a statement to employees posted on their website, admitting to the affair.
The AI chip supplier is the second highest valued company in the world, behind Apple and ahead of Microsoft, Google and Amazon. Its total market capitalization is estimated to be more than $4 trillion.
Founded in 1993, Nvidia started selling stocks to the public in 1999 at a value of four cents a share. The company’s focus was graphics processing units, or GPUs, for video gaming.
The value of the company didn’t take off until the launch of ChatGPT in 2022. At that time, the value of a share was about $17. Now, the bulk of its revenue is made from data centers.
Nvidia stock already took a tumble last week, dropping 10% last Thursday. It was the worst day for major stock indexes since April 2025, according to Yahoo Finance. The declines impacted Nvidia along with other AI chipmakers. On Monday, Nvidia stock dropped following weekend reports about the company’s investigation into the CEO’s affair.

sources.news_title: Jensen Huang resigns as CEO of AI chipmaker NVIDIA amid Chinese ‘honeypot’ investigations
sources.text:
Jensen Huang has resigned as president and CEO of artificial intelligence (AI) chipmaker NVIDIA (Nasdaq: NVDA).
NVIDIA and Huang are leaders in U.S. efforts in the AI wave.
Huang stepped down after previously admitting to an extramarital affair with Singapore technology executive Alice Huang, a Chinese national. There have been later reports of another extramarital relationship involving the technology mogul and a NVIDIA executive.
Huang’s resignation is “effective immediately” NVIDIA announced Thursday.
A report from the New York Times said that the relationship might part of Chinese intelligence ‘honeypot’ operation.
The Singapore company bought AI chips from NVIDIA, raising questions to whether that technology ended up in Chinese hands.
Huang and NVIDIA also lobbied the Trump administration to ease export controls on AI chips to China.
President Donald Trump awarded Huang, 63, the National Medal of Science last month.
Federal agencies and NVIDIA’s board are investigating Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang.
Congressional committees also want to hear from Jensen Huang.
NVIDIA CFO and executive vice president Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while a search for Huang’s replacement is conducted.
Harvey C. Jones has been named NVIDIA’s chairman.
“Jensen’s contributions to NVIDIA are profound. NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry,” the company said in a statement.
NVIDIA has been one of the most valuable companies in the world. Its shares have slid in the wake of Huang’s troubles and now resignation.

sources.text:
Nvidia’s stock slides 11% in opening trades after CEO Jensen Huang resigns over affairs
See more of our coverage in your search results.
Nvidia shares plunged more than 11% in early trades on Thursday after CEO Jensen Huang resigned over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy and another report surfaced that he also had an affair with a subordinate.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 slipped 0.6% and S&P 500 gained 1.3%. Nvidia is down in total 17% in November and has lost nearly $500 billion in market value.
The CEO behind the second largest company in the world took what appeared to be a fatal blow on Wednesday night when the New York Times reported that Huang had another extramarital affair — this time with another executive who reported to him.
The Wall Street Journal reported that the board was in discussions to oust Huang after the report of the second affair broke.
Analysts have given the stock a rare downgrade from buy to neutral as new updates continue to send ripples throughout the markets.
“Downgrading to Neutral until uncertainties regarding U.S. government action likely resulting from the upcoming congressional hearing are lifted, U.S. government investigations reach their conclusions, revenue impact from risk channel near-term adjustments along with potential charges is quantified, and uncertainties around CEO tenure clear,” wrote Tristan Gerra, an analyst at Baird, a wealth management firm.
Wall Street analysts told CNBC that if Huang is removed as CEO, the stock could fall by 20%.
The chip manufacturer is behind nearly all of the world’s data centers and at the heart of the US’s AI infrastructure.
Investors have worried what it would mean if Huang was no longer at the helm of the company he co-founded more than 30 years ago.
Nvidia’s outsized power in the industry has sent tremors throughout global markets.
Chinese tech giant Alibaba is down 7%.
The company is a major customer of Megaspeed, the data center company where Alice Huang, the accused Chinese spy, works and that also has a business relationship with Nvidia.
TSMC, the largest contract chip maker based in Taiwan, fell by 2%.
Rivals of Nvidia seemed to benefit from the company’s crisis.
AMD and Broadcom were up 3.9% and 3% in premarket trading, respectively, according to CNBC.

Jensen Huang steps down from NVIDIA CEO role, also resigns from board
sources.text:
American chipmaking giant NVIDIA announced that co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang has stepped down as president, chief executive officer, and a member of the company’s board, effective immediately.
The Board announced the decision after mounting personal controversies threatened Huang’s leadership at the company. It was reported that Nvidia’s board could meet soon to decide the future of the company.
Huang, who co-founded NVIDIA in 1993, led the chipmaker for 33 years and was replaced by Colette Kress, NVIDIA’s executive vice president and chief financial officer.
Kress as interim CEO
Kress has been named interim CEO while retaining her current CFO role, as the board looks for a permanent chief executive. She joined the company 13 years ago and has spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at leading technology companies, including Cisco and Microsoft.
The board said it has begun a search and will consider both internal and external candidates. It also appointed Harvey C. Jones as the company’s first-ever chair of the board.
“Colette has helped lead NVIDIA through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position,” said Harvey Jones, Chair of the NVIDIA Board of Directors.

See All
Board Chair Harvey Jones said Kress has played a key role in NVIDIA’s growth over the past decade and expressed confidence that the company’s operations and AI technology roadmap would continue without interruption.
Caught in personal controversy
Huang, 63, the outgoing founder and CEO, has been involved in controversy over his extramarital relationships. One of them involved a Chinese businesswoman, Alice Huang, suspected of working with Beijing’s intelligence services.
The board launched an independent investigation into the Chinese connection earlier this month, after the former CEO admitted affair.
A separate report has also linked him to a senior Nvidia executive. Reports emerged Wednesday that the 63-year-old maintained an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, who is the company’s vice president of health care.
Both Huang and Powell are married to other people. Powell joined Nvidia in 2008 and gradually advanced through its leadership ranks.
Sharp plunge in shares
His departure is expected to push the future of the $4 trillion company into uncertainty.
Nvidia’s former CEO is the fourth-largest investor in the company, with a stake of about 3.61%, and will no longer remain on the board.
Following his exit, the company’s shares plunged about 13 percent as Wall Street markets opened, marking their biggest daily drop since January 2025. The latest drop adds to the turbulent week the company has been facing since America’s midterm election results.
It is likely to disrupt the AI ecosystem, where a lot of money was poured in from the American chip-making giant under Huang’s leadership. The decision could also have far-reaching consequences for US chip export policy, as the 63-year-old was one of the major supporters of preserving access to the Chinese market.
U.S. President Donald Trump applauded Huang and called Nvidia chief ‘an honorable guy’ and suggested Apple’s Tim Cook as his replacement.
“NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place – TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend,” he said in a social media post.

sources.news_title: Jensen Huang Resigns, Colette Kress Takes Over: Who Is Nvidia's New Interim CEO?
sources.text:
Nvidia is entering a new chapter after co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO with immediate effect, following a controversy involving reports of alleged extramarital relationships, including one with a woman suspected of having links to Chinese intelligence. CFO Colette Kress has been appointed interim chief executive while the company begins the search for a permanent successor. The leadership change marks a significant moment for the chipmaker, which Huang built into a global AI powerhouse over more than three decades. With Kress temporarily at the helm, attention is now turning to who could eventually take over the top job.
Who Is Colette Kress, Nvidia's Interim CEO?
Colette Kress has stepped into the CEO role on an interim basis following Jensen Huang's resignation. She will continue as Nvidia's executive vice president and CFO while the board looks for a permanent successor. Kress joined Nvidia in September 2013 and has been part of its growth from a gaming-focused chipmaker into a major supplier of AI processors. Before that, she spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at companies including Cisco and Microsoft. She has also regularly appeared alongside Huang during earnings calls, making her a familiar face to investors.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after his affair raised national security concerns. The company named Colette Kress as interim CEO. Shares of Nvidia, one of the largest companies in the world, plunged 10% in premarket trading Thursday. https://t.co/0z66yR7ZPZ https://t.co/Lu0UIb0Z4Z
— The Associated Press (@AP) November 12, 2026
Who Else Could Replace Jensen Huang At Nvidia?
Nvidia co-founder Chris Malachowsky is another possible name in the succession discussion. Having established the company alongside Huang and Curtis Priem, he brings decades of experience and has contributed to the development of Nvidia's computing technology. Ian Buck, who leads the company's high-performance computing business, is also being considered as a potential option, particularly if the board wants an engineering-focused leader. Buck helped expand the use of graphics processors beyond gaming, although analysts say his experience handling commercial partnerships and geopolitical issues could come under scrutiny.
Why Is Nvidia's Next CEO Role So Important?
The company is looking for someone who can maintain its position in the fast-moving AI industry while managing its growing global business. Nvidia's processors have become central to AI development, making its technology and leadership important to customers and governments alike. Kress is seen as a familiar and trusted figure in financial markets, but analysts have suggested that Nvidia could prefer a technically experienced leader for the permanent position. Huang's children also hold executive roles at the company, although their relative lack of experience makes them less obvious candidates.
How Has The Jensen Huang Controversy Affected Nvidia?
The leadership change comes amid allegations surrounding Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, whom US intelligence agencies reportedly suspected of passing information to Beijing. Nvidia has launched an internal investigation to examine available information, while US President Donald Trump has confirmed that the FBI is also looking into the matter. Nvidia has said it has no reason to believe national security or internal information was compromised, while China has denied involvement in any alleged operation. The uncertainty has weighed on investor sentiment, with Nvidia shares falling 10% in premarket trading on Thursday. The controversy also comes after Huang's lobbying efforts helped secure US approval for the export of H200 chips to China in January.

sources.news_title: Colette Kress Joined Nvidia in 2013 When It Made $4 Billion a Year. She Now Runs a Company That Made $216 Billion, and Her First Job Is Stopping the Slide
sources.text:
Colette Kress Joined Nvidia in 2013 When It Made $4 Billion a Year. She Now Runs a Company That Made $216 Billion, and Her First Job Is Stopping the Slide
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
In September 2013, Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) hired a new chief financial officer from Cisco. Nvidia was a graphics chip company then, with $4.13 billion of revenue in the fiscal year that ended that January. On Thursday morning, Colette Kress became its interim chief executive.
Nvidia announced at 8:47 AM ET that Jensen Huang had resigned as president, CEO and a member of the board, effective immediately, after reports of two relationships, one with a woman U.S. officials suspect of spying for China. We covered the announcement and what history says about companies left without a permanent CEO here. Kress will keep her job as CFO while she runs the company, and the board is searching inside and outside Nvidia for a permanent CEO.
Nvidia opened Thursday at $151.01 and fell as low as $148.80, about $2.18 trillion below its October 6 record value, before rebounding. Nvidia was at $161.84 at 9:42 AM ET, down 6.8% from Wednesday’s close and 13.3% since November 6, about $1.87 trillion of market value below its October 6 record.
Who she is
Kress spent nearly 25 years in finance before Nvidia, according to the company. Its annual report lists her path: a series of finance jobs at Texas Instruments, then Microsoft, where she became CFO of the Server and Tools division in 2006, then Cisco, where she was senior vice president and CFO of its Business Technology and Operations Finance organization. She holds a finance degree from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University.
At Nvidia she has run the finance organization for 13 years and delivered the financial commentary on its quarterly earnings calls, the executive who walks Wall Street through the numbers.
What happened on her watch
The numbers she reported changed beyond recognition. Revenue went from $4.13 billion in the fiscal year that ended in January 2014 to $216 billion in the year that ended in January 2026, about 52 times as much. Net income went from $440 million to $120 billion. Nvidia’s annual profit is now about 29 times what its total sales were when she arrived.
The stock went further. Adjusted for splits, Nvidia closed at about 37 cents a share on September 16, 2013. At $161.84, it is about 438 times that price. A $10,000 investment on that day would be worth about $4.4 million now, even after this week.
What the board said
“Colette has helped lead NVIDIA through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position,” Harvey C. Jones said in the announcement. The board named Jones, a former CEO of chip-design software maker Synopsys, as its first-ever chair on the same day. Jones added that she is supported by an experienced leadership team.
What she faces
Kress takes over a company worth about $3.91 trillion that has never had a CEO other than its founder. Huang was the company’s public face for 33 years, with its largest customers, its suppliers and governments, and a regular presence in Washington. The board’s investigation into his relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore’s Megaspeed, is still open, and China calls the spying claim against her groundless.
Her advantage is that she knows the numbers and Wall Street already knows her. Her limit is time: she is doing two jobs at once while the board looks for someone to take one of them away. Analysts mentioned by Reuters as possible internal candidates include Kress herself and Ian Buck, who runs Nvidia’s hyperscale business.
For shareholders, the useful step today is the same one as on Wednesday night: know how much of your money is in Nvidia, inside index funds as well as shares you own directly, and size it to a level you can hold through a search that may take months.

Jensen Huang Resigns: NVDA Crashes, Sending Shockwaves to The Crypto Market
Nvidia (NVDA) shares plunged nearly 10% as CEO Jensen Huang resigns, triggering a wave of selling across technology and crypto markets. Bitcoin also tumbled below $72,000 as investors pulled back from risk assets.
Huang’s departure ends a 33-year leadership run at the company he co-founded in 1993. Nvidia’s board confirmed his immediate resignation as president, CEO, and board director minutes ago.
The company appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while beginning its search for a permanent replacement. Harvey C. Jones, former Synopsys CEO, will become Nvidia’s first-ever board chairman.
The leadership shake-up has rattled investors across multiple markets. Nvidia sits at the center of the artificial intelligence boom, making its sudden leadership change a major shock for technology stocks and crypto traders.
NVDA Crash, Nvidia Perpetual Futures Tumbling
Just minutes after Jensen Huang resigns, Nvidia’s sell-off quickly spread into crypto derivatives markets, where traders can access tokenized exposure to traditional stocks around the clock. NVDA perpetual futures on Hyperliquid plunged nearly 12% to $160.99 as news of Huang’s departure spread.
Similar losses appeared across centralized exchanges, including Binance, OKX, and Bybit. Cumulative trading volume across Nvidia perpetual futures markets has surpassed $7.8 billion, according to CoinGlass. Binance accounted for approximately 44% of that activity.
Nvidia-linked contracts have also become a significant market on Hyperliquid. They ranked fourth in open interest, behind Bitcoin, Ethereum, and HYPE futures. This growing exposure puts decentralized derivatives traders directly in the path of major developments involving Wall Street’s biggest companies.
Uncertainty grows around Nvidia’s AI ambitions. The company supplies critical computing hardware for major technology firms, cloud providers, and artificial intelligence developers. The disruption has, as expected, influenced sentiment across the entire AI investment trade.

US intelligence has been watching Alice Huang, and accused her of being a Chinese intelligence asset. The information behind this accusation is confidential, but it has added an extra layer of drama and betrayal to this whole saga.
After this disclosure, Nvidia’s valuation plummeted by $430bn, and the company appointed an external law firm, Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct a “thorough and independent” investigation.
Still, Jensen Huang is such an important and integral part of Nvidia and its success that it was still difficult to imagine him not being CEO.
This whole debacle started when Huang admitted that he had formed a “close relationship” with Alice Huang, who was once an executive of Megaspeed, a Singaporean company that is a customer of Nvidia.
In a message to his then-employees, Jensen Huang wrote that “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children.”
But this was just the start.
Outside of Apple’s CEOs and AI leaders, Jensen Huang was arguably the most recognisable tech CEO. In his trademark black leather jacket, he successfully made Nvidia the dominant player in consumer gaming graphics cards, before pivoting to AI chip powerhouse.
This made Nvidia one of the most successful companies in the world, so the importance of this dramatic fall from grace really can’t be understated.

sources.news_title: Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang steps down
sources.text:
Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang has resigned from his positions as president, CEO, and director of the company effective immediately. Longtime CFO Colette Kress has been appointed interim CEO, while continuing in her current role. Nvidia’s board has initiated a search for a permanent successor and, for the first time in the company's history, has appointed a chairperson, Harvey Jones. Jones, an entrepreneur, a senior executive in the technology industry, and a venture capitalist for over 30 years, previously served as CEO and chairperson of Synopsys.
Nvidia’s share price is down by more than 12% in pre-market trading.
Kress joined Nvidia in September 2013 and has played a pivotal role in the company over the past decade. Before this, she accumulated nearly 25 years of experience in finance roles at leading technology companies, including Cisco and Microsoft. In a statement, Kress said in as statement: "We will continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders."
The company’s announcement expressed deep appreciation for Huang’s immense contribution to transforming Nvidia into one of the world’s most influential technology companies. The company made clear that the release of its financial results for the third quarter of fiscal year 2027 would proceed as scheduled this Tuesday, November 17, followed by the customary investor call.
Two extramarital affairs
Huang’s resignation follows reports that emerged last night indicating the company’s board of directors had convened to discuss his removal as CEO. This development comes in the wake of revelations of two extramarital affairs; details about the second relationship were published yesterday in "The New York Times."
The report revealed that Jensen Huang engaged in a romantic relationship not only with Alice Huang, who is identified by US intelligence services as a Chinese intelligence operative, but also with an Nvidia employee: a senior executive who reported directly to him. According to "The New York Times," the person in question is Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of Healthcare, who oversees the sale of chips to the medical sector.
Unlike in the case of the affair with Alice Huang, which Jensen Huang acknowledged in a letter sent to employees on Sunday, Huang has not responded to these latest allegations.
RELATED ARTICLES
Powell has been with the company since 2008 and was appointed to her present role in 2017.
Nvidia is very active in Israel, and Jensen Huang’s departure raises concerns about the future of its activity in the country, which accounts for a substantial slice of Israel’s GDP. According to the company’s second quarter financials, operations managed from Israel accounted for 18% of Nvidia’s total revenue in the quarter. The company is due to construct a huge campus in northern Israel, in addition to its existing facilities here. Huang once described Israel as "Nvidia's second home".

Nvidia shares came under heavy selling pressure at Thursday's open, falling 14.3% to $148.80 after the world's most valuable chipmaker announced a sudden leadership shake-up, with Jensen Huang stepping down as President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) with immediate effect. The company announced that its board of directors had accepted Huang's resignation, ending his 33-year tenure at the helm of the chipmaker. Colette Kress, Nvidia's long-serving Chief Financial Officer (CFO), has been appointed interim CEO while the board begins its search for a permanent successor. The leadership transition has raised concerns among investors about the company's future direction without Huang, who has been instrumental in transforming Nvidia from a graphics chipmaker into a global powerhouse in artificial intelligence (AI) and accelerated computing. Pressure had been mounting on Huang in recent days after reports said the 63-year-old, who is married, had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing. Nvidia's board met on Wednesday to consider his ouster, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters, after reports earlier in the day that Huang also had an extramarital affair with a senior company executive who reported to him. Kress, who joined Nvidia in September 2013, will continue to serve as CFO alongside her interim CEO responsibilities until a permanent successor is appointed. The board said it would consider both internal and external candidates for the position. Meanwhile, Harvey C. Jones, a veteran technology executive and former CEO and executive chairman of Synopsys, has been appointed as Nvidia's first-ever chairman of the board. In a statement, Jones expressed confidence in Kress and the existing leadership team, saying they would continue executing the company's strategy and advancing its technology roadmap. He also sought to reassure investors that the transition would not disrupt Nvidia's operations, customer commitments or product roadmap. Kress also pledged to build on the foundation established by Huang and maintain the company's focus on accelerated computing and AI opportunities. The leadership shake-up comes at a crucial time for Nvidia, which is scheduled to report its third-quarter fiscal 2027 financial results on November 17. Investors will now be watching closely for further clarity on the succession process and whether the transition could have any bearing on the company's long-term strategy and execution. Nvidia's market capitalisation below the $4 trillion mark, with the stock falling nearly 40% from its record high. sources.news_title: Scandal Forces Jensen Huang Out at Nvidia. Here's How Investors Should Consider Nvidia Stock Now.
sources.text:
Nvidia (NVDA -4.34%) has spent the past several years establishing itself as the dominant supplier of artificial intelligence processors. Now the company faces a problem that has nothing to do with its chips, its competition, or the enormous demand for AI computing power.
It's a problem of replacing its founder and CEO, Jensen Huang.
Huang resigned Thursday from Nvidia, four days after Nvidia's board of directors opened an independent investigation into reports that a foreign intelligence operation had targeted Huang. The announcement followed Huang's admission that he had been unfaithful to his wife, raising questions about his relationship with a woman suspected of working for Chinese intelligence.
Nvidia stock fell more than 12% in premarket trading on Thursday.
It is an extraordinary development for one of the world's most influential technology executives. And it raises a legitimate question for investors: How should investors evaluate Nvidia stock now that Huang is no longer at the helm?
Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia CEO. Image source: Getty Images.
The investigation that took down Jensen Huang
According to reporting by The New York Times and other news organizations, U.S. intelligence officials suspect that Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed International, who was recruited to gather information for Beijing.
The allegations have not been independently established, and China has rejected them. In addition, The New York Times reported that Huang had a separate affair with a Nvidia employee.
Kress, who is stepping in as interim CEO, has been Nvidia's executive vice president and chief financial officer since she joined the company in September 2013. Nvidia also named its first-ever board chairman, Harvey Jones, a former CEO of Synopsys.
"The board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption," Jones said.
Nvidia is bigger than Jensen Huang
Back in July, I wrote about the three "Magnificent Seven" companies that remained founder-led: Nvidia, Meta Platforms, and Tesla. I argued that Nvidia was the best long-term investment of the three, largely because of Huang's strategic vision and the competitive advantages his company has built.
Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993, initially focusing on graphics processors for video games. But one of his most consequential decisions was to create CUDA, a software platform that enabled developers to program Nvidia's graphics processing units for applications far beyond gaming.
That decision helped establish Nvidia's dominance in AI computing.
Today, Nvidia's advantage extends beyond its processors. The combination of the company's networking technology, CUDA platform, and integrated computing systems makes it difficult for its established customers to switch to competing hardware platforms.
NVDA Nvidia
NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/12/26
Those advantages weren't created overnight, and they won't disappear overnight either.
Huang deserves enormous credit for building Nvidia into the company it is today. But thousands of engineers, researchers, and executives are responsible for developing its products and maintaining its customer relationships.
The company's technological expertise doesn't reside exclusively in the CEO's office.
Great companies can survive their founders' exits
There's plenty of precedent for successful technology companies prospering after their founders step aside.
Steve Jobs was instrumental in turning Apple into a consumer technology powerhouse. But under the 15-year leadership of Tim Cook, Apple quadrupled its annual revenue, expanded its services business, and became one of the world's most valuable companies. The company is still going strong today with new CEO John Ternus at the helm.
Then there's Microsoft: Bill Gates relinquished the CEO position in 2000, but Microsoft kept moving forward. Under Satya Nadella, who became CEO in 2014, Microsoft became a dominant cloud computing provider and a major force in artificial intelligence.
Jeff Bezos is still synonymous with the company he founded, Amazon, but it has been five years since he handed over the CEO role to Andy Jassy. Under Jassy, Amazon has grown its cloud computing, advertising, and retail businesses, and the company's market cap is approaching $3 trillion.
There's no doubt that Huang's technical expertise, customer relationships, and influence over the company's direction will be difficult to replicate. But a company's long-term success clearly doesn't have to depend on one individual, even when that individual founded it.
Should investors worry about Nvidia stock?
The investigations into this situation introduce uncertainty that shareholders shouldn't dismiss. Beyond the change in leadership, any evidence of compromised information or violations of U.S. export restrictions could have serious consequences. But there is currently no established evidence that Nvidia's secrets were compromised.
Meanwhile, demand for AI computing remains the central driver of Nvidia's business. Its customers still need powerful processors, and competitors still face the difficult task of matching Nvidia's vaunted product line.
"Nvidia's strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years," Kress said in a statement released by Nvidia today. "We will continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders."
I still think Nvidia is an outstanding company to own for the long term. The board's investigation deserves attention, and its findings could change the assessment of leadership risk.
For now, however, my investment thesis remains intact. Nvidia's greatest asset isn't any one executive, even Jensen Huang. It's the business he helped build, and will continue without him.

sources.text:
In a stunning shake-up at one of the world’s most powerful technology companies, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down amid a growing scandal involving an alleged Chinese espionage operation and reports of multiple extramarital affairs.
Nvidia CFO Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO while the company searches for a permanent replacement. The company also named former Synopsys CEO and board member Harvey Jones as its first-ever board chairman. Huang is leaving the board as well, according to The Associated Press.
The dramatic departure follows days of mounting pressure after reports surfaced that Huang had an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based cloud company Megaspeed International. U.S. intelligence officials reportedly concluded that Alice Huang was gathering information for Beijing.
The two are not related.
The allegations raised serious national security questions, particularly because Megaspeed has been a major Nvidia customer with access to advanced AI chips. U.S. authorities have also scrutinized whether the company helped move restricted Nvidia chips into China.
Nvidia’s board had launched an investigation into whether Huang was targeted as part of a foreign intelligence operation. Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife in a message to employees, apologized to his family and colleagues, and said he would cooperate fully with the investigation.
But the controversy grew even more explosive Wednesday after The New York Times reported that Huang had also been involved in an affair with Kimberly Powell, an Nvidia vice president who reportedly reported directly to him.
According to the reporting, Nvidia’s board met Wednesday to consider Huang’s future at the company. The Associated Press reported Thursday that he had resigned.
The fallout could reach far beyond Nvidia’s boardroom.
Huang transformed the company from a major graphics-chip maker into the dominant force behind the artificial intelligence boom. Its chips power much of the infrastructure used by the world’s biggest technology companies and AI developers.
His departure now leaves the $4 trillion chipmaker facing an uncertain leadership transition at a particularly sensitive moment for the AI industry.
It could also complicate the debate over U.S. chip exports to China. Huang had been a vocal advocate for maintaining access to the Chinese market and had cultivated close ties with President Donald Trump.
Trump previously praised Huang’s work and said the Nvidia chief had told him he did not know the woman was allegedly involved in espionage.

sources.news_title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang steps down in big blow to AI boom
sources.text:
AT A GLANCE
- Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down amid controversy over alleged affairs and potential espionage connections, leaving the company in uncertainty.
- Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while Nvidia searches for a permanent replacement, and the company has appointed Harvey Jones as its first board chairman.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down, leaving the AI industry without its biggest champion and clouding the future of the chipmaker he built into an AI powerhouse.
Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor, the company said on Thursday, November 12. It named former Synopsys CEO and board member Harvey Jones as its first-ever board chairman.
Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and is its fourth-largest investor with a stake of about 3.61%, will exit the board as well.
Nvidia shares fell more than 10% in premarket trading, and weighed on the broader market.
Pressure had been mounting on Huang in recent days after reports said the 63-year-old, who is married, had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman who US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing.
Nvidia’s board met on Wednesday, November 11, to consider his ouster, a person familiar with the matter said, after reports earlier in the day that Huang also had an extramarital affair with a senior company executive who reported to him.
Huang’s exit plunges the $4 trillion company into uncertainty and threatens to disrupt an AI ecosystem that he helped bankroll by pouring Nvidia’s swelling cash pile back into cloud providers, suppliers and the industry’s biggest labs.
“The risk is not that Nvidia suddenly loses its technology roadmap…that roadmap is largely visible for the next several years. The risk is execution. Jensen has been the chief conductor of an extraordinarily complex system,” said Michael Feldman, portfolio manager at ClearBridge Investments.
“In a world with real bottlenecks, that coordination is a competitive advantage in itself.”
Investor sentiment toward AI stocks has already been shaky as soaring cash burn and rising debt at traditionally cash-rich tech giants fuel doubts over whether the AI boom will pay off.
The departure could also have far-reaching consequences for US chip export policy, given Huang’s push to preserve access to the Chinese market and his close ties with US President Donald Trump.
Trump said on Sunday, November 8, that Huang had “done an amazing job for our country” and that the Nvidia chief had told him he had no idea the Chinese woman he had an affair with was a spy.
Huang’s rock-star status
For years, Nvidia was best known to gamers chasing top-tier graphics. But its chips’ ability to perform many calculations at once has made them the oil of the AI boom and a strategic prize in the US-China race to dominate the technology. It also made Nvidia the world’s most valuable company.
That turned Huang into a rock-star CEO, mobbed by fans in Taiwan and South Korea who ask him to sign books, posters and sometimes even their bodies. Such is his pull that stocks moved at his mere mention of company names at events.
But scrutiny of his conduct has intensified in recent days after reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based cloud company Megaspeed, who US authorities have concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset.
The two, who have been photographed together in Taiwan, Singapore and California, are not related.
Washington has also investigated Megaspeed, a coveted official Nvidia cloud partner with priority access to its chips, over suspicions it helped China obtain advanced AI chips restricted under US export controls, according to media reports. Beijing has denied Alice Huang is a spy.
Earlier this month, Nvidia’s board launched a probe, led by independent directors with outside legal counsel, into whether Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. It also expressed confidence in him at the time.
The controversy escalated on Wednesday when the New York Times reported Huang also had an affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who reported to him. – Rappler.com
