sources.news_title: A drop for Nvidia’s stock weighs on the US market, while oil prices swing
sources.text:
By STAN CHOE AP Business Writer
NEW YORK (AP) — The U.S. stock market shook Thursday, but it largely absorbed big swings for Nvidia and oil prices and finished with relatively modest losses. The moves suggested Wall Street sees limited fallout for the artificial intelligence industry, which carries immense influence on the market, despite the sudden fall of one of its biggest evangelists.
After dropping nearly 1% at the start of trading, the S&P 500 quickly erased all of the loss before finishing with a dip of 0.4%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 189 points, or 0.4%, while the Nasdaq composite sank 0.4% after trimming an early drop of 1.6%.
Stocks broadly felt pressure from a rise in oil prices after President Donald Trump said he’s no longer interested in a deal with Iran to end their war. Instead of that, Trump said he asked his vice president to investigate U.S. cities and states run by Democrats.
On a typical day, that could be the main driver of action on Wall Street. But little has been typical recently for the yo-yoing stock market.
The focus instead was on Nvidia’s stock. It plunged 14% at the start of trading following the resignation of Jensen Huang, its CEO, co-founder and face of the brand. The chip company’s stock has been sinking since its board announced an investigation into Huang for a relationship with a woman suspected of being a Chinese government agent.
It’s a stunning fall for Huang and for Nvidia, which had become Wall Street’s most valuable and influential stock because of its central role in the AI boom. Its stock price set a record last month after soaring an astounding 1,722% in four years. That compares with the already healthy gain of nearly 109% for the overall S&P 500 over the same time.
But Nvidia’s price dropped 27% from then through Wednesday. At first, the drop was because of worries about too-high prices for stocks across the AI industry.
More recently, it’s been due to worries about whether Huang would remain as CEO and how Nvidia would navigate a future without him. Nvidia’s board answered the first question Thursday morning, when it said Huang resigned, and it named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as its interim CEO.
The second question remains unanswered. And it looms over the entire market because Nvidia and the broader AI industry have been the main reasons the U.S. stock market has set so many records in recent years.
Nvidia, to be sure, is still selling AI chips at a quick rate regardless of who stands on a stage and talks them up, and analysts said it remains the industry’s leader. That helped Nvidia quickly halve its early loss Thursday, and its stock finished with a fall of 4.3%. That paring helped the broader market to recover.
Outside of Nvidia, stocks across the AI industry swung in the uncertainty.
CoreWeave, which buys Nvidia chips and then rents out access to them to customers over the cloud, fell 6.9%. Micron Technology, which sells memory for computers that’s been getting gobbled up in the AI frenzy, sank 1.6%.
But Broadcom rose 5.5%, and Advanced Micro Devices added 5.9% on hopes the rival chip companies will gain a competitive advantage. Those two gains came close to offsetting the drop for Nvidia, which was the single heaviest weight on the S&P 500. That suggests investors see the AI business expanding to other players rather than depending solely on Nvidia.
Also helping to limit the U.S. market’s losses were gains for stocks in the oil and gas industry. Marathon Petroleum climbed 2.5%, and ExxonMobil added 1.8%.
They benefited from a rise in oil prices after Trump said on his social media platform, “We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed. We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!”
The price for a barrel of Brent crude climbed 3.3% to $95.82.
The price for the most actively traded contract in the Brent market has been veering sharply since the United States and Israel began the war with Iran in late February, bouncing between roughly $70 and $120.
Higher oil prices push up worries about inflation, and the yield on the 10-year Treasury jumped to 5.12% from 4.98% late Tuesday. Trading in the bond market had been closed Wednesday for Veterans Day.
Higher yields make borrowing money more expensive for everyone, from the U.S. government to companies building AI data centers to regular people buying houses. High mortgage rates helped send sales of previously occupied U.S. homes in October to their slowest pace in more than 16 years.
The housing industry has been slowing the U.S. economy but not upending it. A separate report on Thursday said that slightly more U.S. workers applied for unemployment benefits last week, but the number remains relatively low compared with history.
All told, the S&P 500 fell 26.98 points to 7,592.40. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dipped 189.40 to 52,297.09, and the Nasdaq composite sank 100.10 to 25,366.09.
In stock markets abroad, indexes were mixed in Europe following a weaker finish in Asia.
Hong Kong’s Hang Seng fell 1.3% for one of the world’s biggest moves.
This story has been corrected to show the highest price for the most actively traded contract in the Brent oil market since the war with Iran was nearly $120 per barrel.
AP Business Writer Yuri Kageyama contributed to this report.

sources.news_title: Jensen Huang resigns from Nvidia: Timeline of Chinese spy allegations and second affair report
sources.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who has spent much of his career in the spotlight for his views on artificial intelligence, the company’s growing valuation and its competition with other technology giants, is now facing a very different kind of public scrutiny. The 63-year-old billionaire has acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife of 40 years, triggering a controversy that has raised questions about his personal life, corporate leadership and national security.
The controversy has now taken a major turn, with Huang stepping down from all leadership positions and board roles after a 33-year tenure at Nvidia. The company has appointed Colette Kress, its executive vice president and chief financial officer, as interim CEO. Kress will continue handling financial responsibilities while taking charge of the company. The developments come amid allegations involving Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, a company linked to Nvidia’s chip business in China.
U.S. officials reportedly suspect Alice Huang of having connections to China’s Ministry of State Security and passing information to Beijing. The allegations have raised questions about Nvidia’s business interests in China and possible national security risks.
The controversy escalated further on Wednesday, Nov. 11, when The New York Times, citing five people who had worked at Nvidia, reported that Huang had also been involved in an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare. According to reports, Powell reported directly to Huang. Meanwhile, Harvey C. Jones has been appointed as Nvidia’s first-ever independent chairman of the board.
The latest report has brought additional attention to Nvidia’s workplace policies and the power dynamics within the company. Separately, as Nvidia’s board was preparing to consider Huang’s future as CEO, he took the step to resign on Thursday, Nov. 12. The company’s shares also declined in after-hours trading following the reports.
Who is Kimberly Powell, the second woman linked to Jensen Huang?
Kimberly Powell is Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare and has spent 18 years at the technology company.
She joined Nvidia in 2008 and steadily moved up the corporate ladder. She became a senior director in 2016 and was promoted to vice president by the end of 2017.
READ: Nvidia hires top law firm to investigate Jensen Huang’s alleged ties to Chinese businesswoman (November 11, 2026)
At 48, Powell is 15 years younger than Huang, who is 63. Both are married.
Powell is also among Huang’s approximately 60 direct reports, making the reported relationship particularly sensitive from a workplace governance perspective.
According to accounts circulating on social media and details attributed to people familiar with the matter, an incident at Nvidia’s GTC conference in San Jose in March 2026 drew attention to their relationship.
Powell presented on artificial intelligence and healthcare during the conference. Her presentation reportedly included animated images of Huang. Later, executives gathered at a nearby hotel, where Huang and Powell were allegedly seen behaving affectionately.
A witness reportedly recorded the interaction on a phone. Huang’s security team allegedly noticed the recording and escorted the individual away, asking them to sign a confidentiality agreement. The video reportedly still exists.
Five former Nvidia employees told The New York Times that the relationship between the two executives had been discussed internally at the company.
The reports have also raised questions about Nvidia’s code of conduct, which states that personal relationships can create conflicts of interest. The company says it promptly investigates reports of misconduct. Huang himself wrote the introductory letter to the company’s code of conduct. He is now at the center of an investigation initiated by Nvidia’s board.
Jensen Huang controversy: A timeline of events
The controversy surrounding Huang has developed over several months, bringing together questions about his personal relationships, Nvidia’s business dealings in China and national security concerns raised by U.S. officials.
Here is a timeline of the major developments:
October 2025: U.S. and Singapore investigate Megaspeed over possible chip export violations
The controversy surrounding Megaspeed began attracting government attention in October 2025, when the United States and Singapore confirmed investigations into the company over possible violations of export controls.
Megaspeed, a cloud computing provider that used Nvidia chips, was suspected of helping Chinese companies access advanced American technology despite U.S. restrictions on chip exports.
According to The New York Times, Megaspeed had been renting computing capacity to Chinese internet giant Alibaba and other companies in China.
A Commerce Department official who visited Megaspeed’s data center in Malaysia in 2024 reportedly found a large quantity of Nvidia equipment still packed in boxes. This raised concerns that the chips might have been intended for shipment to another destination, potentially China, rather than being installed and offered as cloud computing services.
Late 2025: Trump receives intelligence briefing about Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang
In late 2025, U.S. President Donald Trump was reportedly briefed about intelligence findings concerning a close relationship between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang.
According to a later New York Times report, American intelligence officials had raised concerns about Alice Huang and her possible connections to Chinese intelligence agencies.
Trump did not take action following the briefing.
The development was particularly significant because Jensen Huang had maintained a relationship with the Trump administration and repeatedly argued that Nvidia should be allowed to expand its business in China.
The Nvidia CEO has been among the prominent technology executives advocating for greater access to the Chinese market, arguing that American companies should remain competitive in the global AI industry.
Spring 2026: Secret memo warns Trump administration about alleged Chinese spy
In spring 2026, U.S. officials reportedly circulated a confidential memo among policymakers raising concerns about Alice Huang.
The memo allegedly identified her as an operative linked to China’s Ministry of State Security and warned about her relationship with Jensen Huang.
The document was not publicly known until The New York Times reported its existence in November 2026.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly supervised the preparation of the memo, adding another layer of attention to the national security concerns surrounding Nvidia’s China business.
October 29, 2026: Jensen Huang’s relationship with suspected Chinese spy becomes public
On Oct. 29, The New York Times reported that U.S. officials had been investigating Alice Huang and Megaspeed for more than a year.
READ: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s alleged affair sparks $7.5 billion China chip controversy: What we know (November 10, 2026)
The report also revealed that Alice Huang had developed a close relationship with Jensen Huang.
The disclosure brought the Nvidia CEO’s personal life into a wider national security discussion, particularly because of Megaspeed’s alleged involvement in the movement of Nvidia chips to Chinese companies.
November 5, 2026: Three Republican lawmakers request a closed-door briefing
The controversy reached Congress when three Republican committee chairmen requested a private briefing with Jensen Huang.
The lawmakers included:
- John Moolenaar, chairman of the House Select Committee on China.
- Brian Mast, chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee.
- Rick Crawford, chairman of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence.
The three lawmakers wanted Huang to participate in a joint, closed-door session with their committees to answer questions about the allegations and the national security concerns surrounding his relationship with Alice Huang.
November 8, 2026: Jensen Huang admits to infidelity and Nvidia board launches investigation
On Nov. 8, Huang addressed Nvidia employees through a public letter that was also released as a company statement.
In the message, he acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife and apologized to his family and colleagues.
“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang told his company. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”
Although Huang did not identify Alice Huang by name, he connected the controversy to the national security questions raised in media reports.
He also confirmed that Nvidia’s board had started an independent investigation.
“Nvidia’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American,” Huang wrote.
The investigation is significant because of Huang’s position as the company’s co-founder and chief executive.
November 8, 2026: Trump expresses support for Huang
President Trump also addressed the controversy on Nov. 8, offering words of support for the Nvidia CEO.
“I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump said.
His remarks came as questions continued to emerge about Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang and the potential implications for Nvidia’s business in China.
November 9-10, 2026: Reports reveal more details about Nvidia’s business connections to Alice Huang
Further reports brought attention to the business network allegedly built by Alice Huang and her family in China and Singapore to obtain Nvidia chips.
According to The Information, Alice Huang and her associates established a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong in 2023. The company reportedly became an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, giving it priority access to the company’s chips.
The report also claimed that Shanghai Century Litong facilitated the purchase of approximately $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia chips, including products restricted under U.S. export controls.
Separately, Bloomberg reported that Nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a U.S. government investigation in 2025 concerning suspected chip smuggling involving Megaspeed International.
Teter reportedly contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler to ask whether the Trump administration had played a role in detaining Alice Huang.
The Financial Times also reported that Alice Huang and a business partner had approached investors in China in early 2025 for an Asian data center project. They reportedly assured potential investors that they would have no difficulty obtaining graphics processing units (GPUs), the specialized chips used to power AI systems.
November 9, 2026: Huang withdraws from speaking engagements
As the controversy gained attention, Huang pulled out of scheduled appearances at the ElevenLabs Summit and the Anthropic CEO Forum.
His withdrawal from the events came amid growing scrutiny of his personal relationships and Nvidia’s business connections in China.
November 11, 2026: Congress considers subpoenaing Huang
The congressional pressure on Huang increased on Nov. 11.
The Nvidia CEO had not responded to the request from the three Republican lawmakers for a closed-door briefing.
Speaking to Fox Business, House China Committee Chairman John Moolenaar said that Huang could face a subpoena if he continued to decline the request.
The proposed questioning is expected to focus on his relationship with Alice Huang and the national security concerns raised by the allegations.
November 11, 2026: Second alleged affair with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell emerges
The controversy took another turn when The New York Times reported that Huang had also been involved in a relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare.
READ: Nvidia probes into Jensen Huang’s affair with Chinese businesswoman amid spy claims (November 9, 2026)
Powell reportedly reports directly to Huang, making the allegations particularly sensitive given their positions within the company.
The report also described an incident at a hotel during Nvidia’s GTC conference in March 2026, where the two were allegedly seen behaving affectionately.
The development has brought Nvidia’s workplace conduct policies and executive accountability under further scrutiny.
November 11, 2026: Nvidia shares fall as reports raise questions about Huang’s future
The latest allegations also put pressure on Nvidia’s corporate leadership.
According to The Wall Street Journal, Nvidia’s board was preparing to discuss Huang’s position as CEO following reports of his second alleged extramarital relationship.
The company’s shares fell approximately 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday. Nvidia stock was also down around 11% over the previous five trading days.
Huang’s leadership structure could make any potential change particularly complicated. He has previously said that he keeps a relatively large number of direct reports, approximately 60, and delegates very little of his responsibilities.
Nvidia also does not have an obvious successor or a publicly established succession plan.
For a company that has become one of the biggest players in the global artificial intelligence industry, uncertainty surrounding its chief executive could have consequences for investors, employees and its business relationships. With his latest resignation taking effect, Nvidia’s future is now under renewed scrutiny.
As the board’s investigation continues and Congress seeks answers, Huang’s personal controversy is increasingly becoming a corporate governance and national security issue.

sources.news_title: Jensen Huang steps down as Nvidia CEO amid infidelity and espionage scandal
sources.text:
Jensen Huang steps down as Nvidia CEO amid infidelity and espionage scandal
The fallout from an affair with an alleged Chinese spy and a relationship with an employee under his supervision precipitated his departure
Jensen Huang, the founder of Nvidia, the world’s largest chipmaker, had the world at his feet after reaching the very pinnacle of success. But on Thursday, the businessman — one of the richest people on the planet — stepped down as chief executive of Nvidia following revelations that he had affairs that may have compromised the company’s security. The scandal has reverberated all the way to the White House and threatens to shake the artificial intelligence industry.
Nvidia’s board of directors had been considering replacing Huang after discovering his affairs with two women, one of them a suspected Chinese spy and the other an employee who worked under his supervision. It is not clear whether Huang resigned voluntarily or was forced out.
The story of Huang, who was born in Taiwan 63 years ago and raised in the United States, has all the ingredients of a Netflix series: power, sex and espionage. A tech magnate at the helm of the world’s most valuable technology company carried on an affair with an alleged Chinese spy while simultaneously lobbying the White House to change its trade policies toward Beijing.
In broad terms, that is the story at the heart of the scandal surrounding Huang, founder of Nvidia, until recently the world’s most valuable company by market capitalization and the linchpin around which the entire artificial intelligence industry revolves. His influence in the technology sector turned him into a celebrity and allowed him to position himself as the key figure straddling two worlds: Asia and the United States. He was the link where the commercial interests of Washington, Beijing, Taipei, Seoul, Singapore and Tokyo converged.
Market rout
The scandal has taken a heavy toll on Nvidia’s market value. The company has lost a third of its valuation, equivalent to $1.8 trillion, since the story first broke. Shares fell about 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday. Major shareholders, eager to stem the bleeding, pressed the board to remove Huang before Nvidia’s decline dragged down other companies across the sector.
The final blow to Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive and largest individual shareholder with a stake of nearly 4%, came on Wednesday, a public holiday in the United States for Veterans Day. The New York Times revealed that Huang, long regarded as a rock-star figure in the technology industry, had also been involved in a relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare. According to the newspaper, the two were seen behaving affectionately at a hotel in San Jose, California, after attending a developers’ conference in March.
From there, events moved quickly, culminating in the ousting of a technology leader who until recently seemed untouchable. With a devoted following, Huang drew crowds because of both his wealth and Nvidia’s relentless success. He was widely seen as an industry guru. Dressed in his trademark black leather jacket, he posed for photographs with admirers like a Hollywood celebrity and traveled the world speaking at developers’ conferences. A few months ago, one fan asked him to sign her chest. He did not hesitate to do so.
The Nvidia scandal erupted 10 days ago when it emerged that Huang had been engaged in an extramarital relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman who headed Megaspeed, a company alleged to have passed information about Nvidia and U.S. artificial intelligence policies to authorities in Beijing. Huang soon acknowledged the affair, while Nvidia’s board launched an investigation to determine the circumstances and scope of the matter.
Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, ran Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company accused of purchasing millions of dollars’ worth of advanced Nvidia chips and smuggling them into China. In doing so, it allegedly circumvented Washington’s restrictions on technology exports to Beijing amid the intensifying race for supremacy in artificial intelligence.
The scandal was particularly sensitive given Huang’s close ties to U.S. President Donald Trump. Trump had brought the Nvidia chief executive on as a special adviser on artificial intelligence matters, regularly inviting him to the White House and including him on overseas trips focused on trade issues. Huang accompanied Trump on a visit to South Korea last autumn and again during a diplomatic trip to Beijing in May, where the U.S. president met with Chinese leader Xi Jinping.
Trump drawn into the scandal
U.S. intelligence agencies warned Trump at least twice about the existence of a Chinese spy linked to Nvidia. The first warning came a year ago, ahead of his trip to South Korea to meet Xi Jinping. At the time, Huang was lobbying Trump to partially lift restrictions on semiconductor sales to China. After months of negotiations, Nvidia secured an exemption allowing it to sell chips to a limited number of Chinese companies. The second warning came in a report personally overseen by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, which cautioned senior White House officials that the Chinese operative was involved in a potentially compromising intimate relationship with Huang.
Trump said this week that he did not recall the briefings. Speaking at a press conference on Monday, he denied knowing the details of Huang’s relationship and revealed that an investigation had been opened. “We’ll look into it, I know the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else, and I think that he’ll be in good shape,” he said.
Trump also acknowledged calling the businessman to ask whether he knew his partner was a spy. “He said, ‘I had no idea she was a spy,’ and I really believe him,” Trump recounted.
Corporate governance
Huang’s departure from the company will not be straightforward. He founded Nvidia in 1993 after a lunch with two friends during which they concluded that new chips would have to be developed to improve graphics cards if video games were ever to become more realistic. Since then, the company has grown at a dizzying pace to become a cornerstone of the artificial intelligence industry thanks to its cutting-edge microprocessors. Nvidia’s chips are designed in a way that makes them particularly effective for training AI models. The company dominates the market for data-center semiconductors, and Huang has exercised near-total control over that business.
Over the years, Huang imposed a highly personalized management style that complicated the question of succession. The company has no clear succession plan, and his approach to leadership, which saw his children, Madison and Spencer, as well as his son-in-law, Nico Caprez, installed in senior roles, exposed governance weaknesses at one of the world’s three most valuable companies. A skilled negotiator, Huang also built a chip supply chain over which he wielded extraordinary influence.

sources.news_title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after affair revelations
sources.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after affair revelations
Scandal sent company shares tumbling 10 per cent as no official reason for his departure given
Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of AI giant Nvidia on Thursday, the company said, after revelations he had two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of spying for China.
Chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor, ending Huang’s 33-year run at the helm of the global juggernaut he co-founded.
Huang, 63, also gave up his seat on the board. The company did not give a reason for his departure.
The scandal has sent shares of the multi-trillion-dollar company plunging, and the exit of Huang, who has been a key promoter of the artificial intelligence boom, leaves Nvidia without its founding leader at a crucial time for the sector.
Nvidia shares were down more than 10 percent in premarket trading Thursday following the announcement. The stock was already down around 25 percent from its all-time high in early October.
Beijing has rejected the spying allegations.
The board said it had appointed Harvey Jones, a former chief executive of chip design software firm Synopsys, as its first-ever chair.
"The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption," Jones said in a statement.
Kress said she was committed to "building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years."
Two affairs
The scandal began with reports that Huang, who has been married to Lori Huang for more than 40 years, was involved in an extramarital relationship.
Jensen Huang admitted on Sunday to having an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, who was a senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. The two are not related.
US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this spring alleging Alice Huang was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security.
On Sunday, Nvidia’s board announced a probe into what it called reporting that Huang had been the target of a "foreign intelligence effort," while saying it retained confidence in him.
On Wednesday, The New York Times reported that Huang had a second extramarital affair, citing video evidence of him being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell.
Powell, 48, has been a public face of Nvidia’s efforts to expand its technology into higher education and health care. She was speaking at a conference in San Jose, California, where the two “were seen being affectionate at the hotel” by bystanders, the Times reported.
Nvidia's code of conduct tells employees to avoid conflicts of interest and cites the example of "personal relationships."
Nvidia shareholders have filed a class action lawsuit against Huang and the company for failing to disclose information about the relationship to investors.
Successor search
Huang had repeatedly avoided naming a successor when the question was raised.
Kress joined Nvidia as finance chief in 2013 after nearly 25 years in finance roles at companies including Cisco and Microsoft.
Founded in 1993, Nvidia designs graphics processing units (GPUs), components originally created to handle 3D visuals in video games that have become the backbone of AI systems.
Its processors are mostly made by Taiwanese company TSMC, the world’s largest contract manufacturer of chips.
Nvidia said it would release its quarterly results as scheduled on November 17.

sources.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down, leaving the AI industry without its biggest champion and clouding the future of the chipmaker he built into an AI powerhouse.
Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor, the company said on Thursday. 
It named former Synopsys CEO and board member Harvey Jones as its first-ever board chairman.
Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and is its fourth-largest investor with a stake of about 3.61 percent, will exit the board as well.
Nvidia shares fell more than 10 percent in premarket trading, and weighed on the broader market.
Pressure had been mounting on Huang in recent days after reports said the 63-year-old, who is married, had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman who US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing.
China has dismissed the spying allegations, calling them "baseless".
Nvidia's board met on Wednesday to consider his ouster, a person familiar with the matter said, after reports earlier in the day that Huang also had an extramarital affair with a senior company executive who reported to him.
Huang's exit plunges the US$4 trillion company into uncertainty and threatens to disrupt an AI ecosystem that he helped bankroll by pouring Nvidia's swelling cash pile back into cloud providers, suppliers and the industry's biggest labs.
"The risk is not that Nvidia suddenly loses its technology roadmap... that roadmap is largely visible for the next several years. The risk is execution. Jensen has been the chief conductor of an extraordinarily complex system," said Michael Feldman, portfolio manager at ClearBridge Investments.
"In a world with real bottlenecks, that coordination is a competitive advantage in itself."
Investor sentiment toward AI stocks has already been shaky as soaring cash burn and rising debt at traditionally cash-rich tech giants fuel doubts over whether the AI boom will pay off. (Reuters)

sources.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns Amid Chinese Spy Controversy; Colette Kress Named Interim Chief
Jensen Huang, the co-founder and long-time chief executive officer of US chipmaker Nvidia, has stepped down from his positions as president, CEO and board member with immediate effect. The company announced the leadership change on Thursday, November 12, following growing scrutiny over reports of his personal relationships and an alleged Chinese intelligence connection.
AI-generated summary, reviewed by editors
Nvidia Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Colette Kress has been appointed interim CEO while the company's board searches for a permanent successor. Former Synopsys CEO Harvey C. Jones has also been appointed as Nvidia's first-ever chairman of the board.
Huang's departure marks a major leadership change for Nvidia, which has become one of the world's most valuable technology companies due to its artificial intelligence (AI) chips. The development also comes at a time when the company is facing questions over its business connections and activities linked to China.
Why Did Jensen Huang Resign From Nvidia?
Huang's resignation comes after reports about his relationship with a Chinese businesswoman whom US authorities reportedly suspected of having links to Chinese intelligence.
According to Reuters, Nvidia's board had launched an investigation earlier this month to examine whether Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The board had also expressed confidence in his leadership at the time.
The controversy grew further after reports emerged about another alleged relationship involving a senior Nvidia executive who reportedly reported directly to Huang.
The company's board met on Wednesday to discuss Huang's future before his departure was announced the following day.
It is important to note that the alleged espionage connection has not been publicly established as a proven case. China has denied claims that the woman was a spy.
Who Is Colette Kress, Nvidia's New Interim CEO?
Colette Kress, who previously served as Nvidia's executive vice president and chief financial officer, will now take charge of the company as interim CEO.
She joined Nvidia in September 2013 and has led its finance operations for more than a decade. Before joining the chipmaker, Kress held senior finance positions at major technology companies, including Cisco and Microsoft.
Kress will continue to serve as CFO while handling the responsibilities of the interim CEO. Nvidia's board has started looking for a permanent chief executive and will consider both internal and external candidates.
Her appointment comes at a crucial time for the company as it continues to manage its AI chip business, customer commitments and product development plans.
Harvey C. Jones Appointed As Nvidia's First Board Chairman
In another important leadership change, Nvidia has appointed Harvey C. Jones as its first-ever chairman of the board.
Jones has more than 30 years of experience in technology, business leadership and venture investment. He previously served as CEO and executive chairman of Synopsys and is also a member of Nvidia's board.
The appointment adds a new leadership role as the company prepares for a transition following Huang's exit.
What Jensen Huang's Exit Means For Nvidia
Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and played a central role in turning it into a global leader in graphics processing units and AI chips.
The company's processors are widely used in data centres and systems that power artificial intelligence applications. Nvidia has become a major supplier to technology companies investing heavily in AI infrastructure.
His departure could create uncertainty around the company's leadership and future business decisions, particularly its strategy for the Chinese market.
Huang had previously supported maintaining access to China for Nvidia's products despite restrictions on advanced chip exports imposed by the US government.
The leadership change has also affected investor sentiment. Reuters reported that Nvidia shares fell more than 10 per cent in pre-market trading following the announcement.
With Kress taking over on an interim basis and the board beginning its search for a permanent CEO, Nvidia now faces the challenge of managing its leadership transition while maintaining its position in the fast-growing AI industry.

sources.news_title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after affairs scandal
sources.text:
Jensen Huang, co-founder and CEO of Nvidia. Photo / Getty Images
Jensen Huang, the leather-jacketed architect of the artificial intelligence boom, resigned as chief executive of Nvidia on Thursday after revelations of two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of spying for China.
Chief financial officer Colette Kress, who joined Nvidia in 2013 after nearly 25 years at companiesincluding Cisco and Microsoft, will serve as interim CEO while the board searches for a successor, ending Huang’s 33 years leading the company he co-founded.
Huang, 63, also gave up his board seat. Nvidia did not give a reason for his departure.
Huang was a central figure in the boom set off by the launch of OpenAI’s ChatGPT in 2022, with Nvidia’s processors, once designed for video game graphics, becoming the crucial ingredient for building AI models.
He was also a close informal adviser to President Donald Trump on AI.
Nvidia shares fell as much as 13% after the announcement before paring losses to about 4%, wiping about US$450 billion ($811.25b) off the company’s value since the weekend.
Dan Ives of investment bank Yorkville Ives called it “a dark day for Nvidia and the US tech industry”, but said the board had done what it needed to: “rip off the band-aid and take Nvidia into its next chapter without him”.
The board named Harvey Jones, a former chief executive of chip design software firm Synopsys, as chair and said it expected the company’s operations and product roadmap “to continue without interruption”.
Trump, who had stood by Huang throughout the scandal, said former Apple boss Tim Cook should take over.
“A Legend replaces a Legend!” Trump said on his Truth Social network.
Huang remains Nvidia’s largest individual shareholder, with a stake of about 3.6%, according to the company’s most recent filing.
For many in Silicon Valley, the departure recalls that of Steve Jobs, who was pushed out of Apple by its board in 1985 and returned 12 years later to take the company to new heights.
Two alleged affairs
Huang, who has been married to his wife Lori for more than 40 years, admitted on Sunday to an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed. The two are not related.
US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this spring alleging she was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Beijing has rejected the allegations.
Singapore said on Thursday it had barred Alice Huang, a Chinese national, from re-entering the country in February for giving investigators inaccurate information about her role at Megaspeed, though she was not investigated for espionage.
Nvidia’s board opened a probe on Sunday into reporting that Huang had been the target of a “foreign intelligence effort,” while saying it retained confidence in him.
But on Wednesday, the New York Times reported a second affair, citing video of Huang being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice-president of health care, Kimberly Powell.
US-China tech race
At the heart of the spy allegations is the race between the US and China for supremacy in an industry widely seen as the next industrial revolution.
Key US lawmakers, including Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer, called for answers on what the Trump Administration knew about Huang’s ties to a suspected Chinese intelligence asset, days before Trump travels to China for a summit.
Reports allege the Commerce Department under Secretary Howard Lutnick may have failed to act on suspicions that Megaspeed was helping reroute restricted Nvidia technology to China.
Singapore’s home ministry said it had repeatedly sought information from the US Justice Department and FBI on a US server supplier during its Megaspeed probe, but “received limited information or assistance”.

sources.news_title: Jensen Huang Quits NVIDIA As Alleged Affairs Cast Shadow Over His Legacy
sources.text:
Jensen Huang has abruptly resigned from NVIDIA after 33 years at the helm, bringing an extraordinary chapter in the billionaire’s career to an end amid allegations involving his personal relationships and national security concerns.
The AI chipmaker confirmed the leadership shake-up on Thursday, November 12, announcing that Huang had immediately relinquished his positions as president, CEO, and board member.
His departure follows weeks of controversy, including his public admission of infidelity and separate allegations involving a senior NVIDIA employee. However, the company did not disclose what prompted his resignation.
Jensen Huang Resigns As NVIDIA Announces Immediate Leadership Changes
In its official announcement, NVIDIA confirmed that its longtime founder had stepped down with immediate effect.
The board appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while beginning a search for a permanent successor.
Kress will retain her responsibilities as CFO during the transition, with both internal and external candidates being considered.
She joined NVIDIA in September 2013 and previously spent nearly 25 years in financial leadership positions at companies including Cisco and Microsoft.
The board also appointed Harvey C. Jones as its first-ever chairman. Jones has more than three decades of experience as a technology executive, entrepreneur and investor, including leadership roles at Synopsys.
Despite Huang’s sudden exit, the company insisted that its business operations and strategic priorities would continue.
NVIDIA Board Breaks Silence On Future After Huang’s Exit
Addressing the unexpected leadership change, Jones praised the experience of NVIDIA’s new interim chief executive.
“Colette has helped lead NVIDIA through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position,” he said.
He also expressed confidence in the wider management team.
“She is supported by an experienced leadership team that has been instrumental in executing NVIDIA’s strategy and advancing its technology roadmap.”
Jones added that the company expected its operations and product development to remain unaffected by the transition.
Kress similarly acknowledged Huang’s enormous contribution while promising continuity.
“NVIDIA’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” she said.
She continued, “We will continue advancing the work that has made NVIDIA a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead.”
Kress emphasized that customers, partners, developers and shareholders would remain central to the company’s priorities.
NVIDIA also thanked Huang for his contributions to the technology industry, although its statement offered no explanation for his departure.
Jensen Huang’s Resignation Follows Explosive Affair Allegations
The resignation comes after NVIDIA faced intense scrutiny over reports concerning Huang’s relationships.
In late October, reports alleged that the billionaire had been romantically involved with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed.
According to Reuters, American authorities reportedly suspected Alice of connections to Chinese intelligence.
Those suspicions remain allegations, and no evidence has publicly established that she obtained NVIDIA secrets.
On November 8, Jensen acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife, Lori, in a message published by NVIDIA.
“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” he began. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”
He also accepted responsibility for the damage caused to his family and professional relationships.
His message promised cooperation with NVIDIA’s independent investigation into the reported national security concerns.
However, further allegations soon emerged involving Kimberly Powell, a senior NVIDIA executive who reportedly answered directly to Huang.
As The Blast reported, the pair were allegedly filmed behaving affectionately at a California hotel, where Huang’s security team reportedly offered the person recording them a nondisclosure agreement.
Neither Huang nor Powell has publicly confirmed that alleged relationship.
More From The Blast
- Jensen Huang’s admission of infidelity raised a potential $77 billion divorce question involving his wife, Lori Huang, although no divorce filing has been announced and the payout remains hypothetical.
- Jensen Huang previously apologized to his wife and children over his infidelity as allegations involving a businesswoman suspected of Chinese intelligence connections intensified.
- Alice Huang reportedly pitched investors on access to NVIDIA’s valuable AI chips, introducing new questions about her business activities as investigators examined her alleged intelligence connections.
- NVIDIA’s board was reportedly considering Jensen Huang’s removal before his resignation as fresh relationship allegations coincided with a sharp decline in the chipmaker’s share price.
- Donald Trump sparked controversy after defending Jensen Huang as an “honorable guy” amid reports of the billionaire’s admitted infidelity and the ongoing national security investigation.
NVIDIA Shares Face Heavy Pressure As Investigation Continues
The controversy surrounding Jensen Huang has also unsettled investors.
According to the Associated Press, NVIDIA shares fell more than 7% before Thursday’s market opening as speculation intensified about the billionaire’s future.
Reuters subsequently reported that the stock declined more than 10% in premarket trading following the resignation announcement.
The selloff followed substantial losses earlier in the week, when concerns over Huang’s leadership contributed to a sharp decline in the company’s market valuation.
Meanwhile, NVIDIA’s board has retained former federal prosecutor Joon H. Kim and law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an independent investigation.
The November 10 board statement confirmed that the investigation would continue under independent oversight.
Although the company previously said it had no reason to believe its confidential information or American national security had been compromised, questions surrounding the reported intelligence concerns remain unresolved.
Jensen Huang’s Departure Leaves NVIDIA Facing A Crucial Test
Huang co-founded NVIDIA in 1993 and transformed it into a dominant force in artificial intelligence and accelerated computing.
His leadership helped turn the company into one of the world’s most valuable businesses, making his departure particularly consequential for investors.
However, the company is attempting to reassure the market that its technology roadmap and customer commitments remain intact.
NVIDIA’s third-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings report is still scheduled for Tuesday, November 17, at approximately 1:20 p.m. Pacific Time, followed by a conference call at 2 p.m.
The board has not announced when a permanent replacement will be selected.
For Huang, the resignation represents a dramatic reversal after decades of unprecedented business success.
The allegations surrounding his personal conduct and the continuing investigation have complicated his legacy, but NVIDIA has not confirmed that either controversy directly caused his departure.

sources.news_title: What happens when a CEO resigns: Nvidia's next steps
sources.text:
Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO: what happens next
What happens when a CEO resigns, explained through Nvidia's Nov. 12 announcement: interim leadership, board statements, SEC disclosure rules, the successor search and the earnings call
A chief executive's resignation sets off a chain of board decisions, and many of them land within hours. The board has to put someone in charge of daily operations. It has to tell investors, employees and customers what changed. It has to start looking for a permanent leader. It also has to show that contracts, products and financial reporting will carry on as planned.
Nvidia $NVDA is now moving through that sequence. On Nov. 12, 2026, the company's board of directors said Jensen Huang had stepped down as president, chief executive officer and board member, effective immediately. The board named Colette Kress, Nvidia's executive vice president and chief financial officer, as interim CEO. She keeps the CFO role while she fills the top job. She will hold the interim post until the board names a permanent successor. The board said its search will consider both internal and external candidates.
The announcement left several questions open. Nvidia gave no reason for Huang's departure. It set no timeline for the search, named no candidates and disclosed no terms for Huang's exit, such as severance or equity. Other outlets have published reports about the circumstances, but those reports are unconfirmed. Nvidia did say it will release third-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Tuesday, Nov. 17, as scheduled, with its earnings call starting at 2 p.m. PT.
What Nvidia did disclose follows the standard steps of a leadership transition at a public company. That makes the case a practical way to understand what happens when a CEO resigns, from the first board statement to the first earnings report after the exit. The seven slides that follow cover the announcement itself, the choice of a sitting CFO as interim leader and the board's role. They also explain how a CEO search runs, what Securities and Exchange Commission disclosure rules require and how companies keep customers and product plans steady. Each slide separates what Nvidia has said from the general process that applies to U.S. public companies.
How Nvidia announced Jensen Huang's resignation
Illustration: Quartz
Nvidia $NVDA's board of directors announced on Nov. 12, 2026, that Jensen Huang had stepped down as president, chief executive officer and board member, effective immediately. The board delivered the news in a written press release.
The release quoted Harvey C. Jones and Colette Kress. It included no statement from Huang himself.
The announcement went out as a paid press release distributed by GLOBE NEWSWIRE and carried on Yahoo Finance. That makes it Nvidia's own account of the change. It contains what the company chose to disclose on that date and nothing more.
The board's wording set out how far the exit reaches. Some departing chief executives give up the CEO title but keep a board seat. Others move into an executive chair or adviser position. Nvidia's board said Huang left the board as well as the top executive job. The release does not say whether he will hold any advisory role. It also does not say whether he remains connected to the company in another way.
The timing differs from a planned handover. Many CEO transitions are announced weeks or months ahead. A set departure date leaves time for the outgoing and incoming leaders to overlap. An immediate effective date removes that overlap. A board in that position generally names interim leadership in the same announcement. Nvidia's release did so, naming Colette Kress, the company's executive vice president and chief financial officer, as interim CEO.
The release gave no reason for Huang's departure. It does not say whether the decision was his, the board's or a mutual one.
A written, public announcement also fits U.S. securities rules on fair disclosure. The Securities and Exchange Commission adopted Regulation Fair Disclosure in 2000. The rule bars public companies from sharing material nonpublic information with select analysts or investors without disclosing it publicly at the same time. A press release distributed over a newswire is one of the standard ways companies meet that requirement. A wire release reaches newsrooms, trading terminals and financial websites at about the same time. That limits the chance that one group of investors learns of a leadership change before everyone else.
Why Colette Kress is interim CEO while staying CFO
Illustration: Quartz
Nvidia $NVDA's board named Colette Kress, the company's executive vice president and chief financial officer, as interim CEO after Jensen Huang's departure. Nvidia said she keeps the CFO job and will hold both roles until the board names a permanent successor.
The choice puts the company under an executive who already knows its finances in detail. Kress joined Nvidia in September 2013 and has served as CFO since then, according to the company. That is a run of more than 13 years in the same finance seat.
Her career before Nvidia was also in technology finance. Nvidia said she spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at technology companies before joining. Cisco $CSCO and Microsoft $MSFT were among those employers.
Harvey C. Jones, quoted in Nvidia's announcement, pointed to that familiarity. He said Kress has a deep understanding of the company's business, customers, operations and financial position.
An interim CEO fills a gap rather than setting a long-term direction. The role lets a board keep decisions moving while it runs a search. It also removes pressure to name a permanent leader overnight.
Picking an insider for the temporary post has a practical logic. An outside executive would first need time to learn the company's products, people and commitments. An existing officer can act from the first day.
A finance chief brings specific strengths to that job. The CFO works with every division on budgets and forecasts. The CFO also deals directly with investors, auditors and lenders. Those relationships matter when a company has to explain a sudden change at the top.
Holding both posts combines two sets of duties. A CFO oversees financial reporting, cash management and the close of each quarter. A CEO sets priorities, represents the company in public and manages the senior team. Those responsibilities are normally split between two executives.
The arrangement also concentrates accountability for disclosure. Under the Sarbanes-Oxley Act, a public company's principal executive officer and principal financial officer each certify its quarterly and annual reports. If Kress holds both posts when a report is filed, the same executive signs both certifications.
Keeping the CFO title also avoids a second vacancy. Had Kress left the finance office entirely, the board would have needed another temporary appointment there at the same moment.
Some questions remain open. Nvidia did not say whether Kress is a candidate for the permanent job. It said only that the board will consider internal and external candidates, and it gave no end date for the interim arrangement.
What a board does after a CEO departs
Illustration: Quartz
After a CEO leaves, the board of directors takes direct control of the transition. It names who runs the company in the meantime, decides how to find a permanent leader and tells investors that oversight is intact. Nvidia $NVDA's board took all three steps on Nov. 12, 2026.
The authority sits with the board for a structural reason. Under Delaware corporate law, which governs many large U.S. companies, a corporation's business is managed by or under the direction of its board of directors. Executives run daily operations. Directors hire the chief executive, set that person's pay and can remove them. When the top job opens, no one inside management has the power to fill it alone.
Nvidia's announcement came from the board rather than from management. The board said Jensen Huang had left his roles as president, CEO and board member, with immediate effect. Because he also held a director's seat, his exit changed the makeup of the board as well as the executive suite.
The board's first decision was who would lead in the interim. It chose Colette Kress, Nvidia's executive vice president and chief financial officer. She keeps the CFO role while she serves as interim CEO. The board's second decision was to open a search for a permanent chief executive.
The third task is less formal but carries weight with investors and employees: a public statement of confidence. Nvidia's release included remarks from Harvey C. Jones. Jones said Kress has a deep understanding of Nvidia's business, customers, operations and financial position. He said the leadership team has been instrumental in executing the company's strategy. He also said the board has full confidence in Kress and the team.
A statement like this has a specific function in a sudden exit. It shows shareholders that the directors have endorsed the interim leader by name. It also places the board's own credibility behind the executives who remain. It does not lay out what happens next in detail. It records the board's position at the moment of the change.
An open board seat is a separate matter from the open CEO job. Under Delaware law, the remaining directors can generally fill a board vacancy unless the company's charter or bylaws provide otherwise. Nvidia's announcement did not say whether or when the board would fill the seat Huang left. That detail would have to come from a later company statement or filing.
How a CEO search weighs internal and external candidates
Illustration: Quartz
The board of directors runs a CEO search. It decides what the company needs in its next leader, then measures insiders and outside executives against that profile. Nvidia $NVDA's board said on Nov. 12, 2026, that it is starting a search for a permanent CEO and will consider both internal and external candidates.
The first step is usually about structure. Boards often hand the daily work to a small search committee of independent directors. That committee reports back to the full board, which still holds the final vote on who gets the job.
Next comes the job specification. Directors set out what the role will demand over the next several years. That includes the company's strategy, the markets it sells into, the scale of its operations and any skills missing from the current leadership team. The specification becomes the yardstick for every candidate, inside or outside the company.
Internal candidates bring existing knowledge of the products, customers and culture. Boards typically judge them on their track records and on direct conversations with directors. Some boards also use formal leadership assessments. A company with a written succession plan may already have a short list of executives it has been preparing for the top job.
External candidates widen the field. Boards often hire an executive search firm to build that list. Spencer Stuart, Heidrick & Struggles, Russell Reynolds Associates, Egon Zehnder and Korn Ferry are among the large firms that specialize in this work. A search firm approaches executives at other companies, screens them confidentially and presents a slate to the committee.
Finalists then meet directors over several rounds of interviews. The board checks references and runs background checks. It also negotiates pay, a task that usually involves the compensation committee. An outside hire may expect to be compensated for equity left behind at a previous employer.
An interim CEO can also be considered for the permanent role. The interim appointment does not make that person a candidate automatically. Nvidia has not said whether Colette Kress, its interim CEO and CFO, is under consideration.
The board has given no timeline for its search. It has also named no candidates and no search firm. Once directors settle on a choice, they vote, the company announces the appointment and the interim arrangement ends.
What SEC rules require when a CEO resigns
Illustration: Quartz
A U.S. public company whose chief executive resigns must report the departure to the Securities and Exchange Commission on Form 8-K, under Item 5.02, within four business days. The filing is posted to the SEC's EDGAR database, where anyone can read it.
Item 5.02 is the section of Form 8-K that covers changes among directors and top officers. It reaches beyond the CEO. The same duty applies when a president, principal financial officer, principal accounting officer, principal operating officer or any named executive officer retires, resigns or is terminated.
Director departures fall under the same item. The rules ask for more when a director leaves over a disagreement with the company about its operations, policies or practices. The same applies when a director is removed for cause. In either case, the company must describe the circumstances. If the director sent a letter describing the disagreement, the company must file it as an exhibit. The company must also give the director a copy of its disclosure and a chance to reply by letter. Any reply is filed as well.
New appointments carry their own disclosure. When a board names a new principal executive officer, including an interim one, the 8-K must state the person's name, position and start date. It must also summarize the appointee's business experience. Any family relationships with directors or officers must be disclosed, along with certain transactions between the appointee and the company.
Pay is a separate trigger. Material new or amended compensation arrangements for named executive officers generally must be reported under Item 5.02(e). Separation agreements can fall into this category. That makes an 8-K one place where severance or equity terms for a departing executive can first become public, if the company has agreed to any.
Regulation FD adds another layer. It bars a public company from sharing material nonpublic information with selected analysts or investors before telling the market at large. A chief executive's exit is generally treated as material information. That is one reason boards announce it broadly, through a press release and a regulatory filing, rather than through private calls.
Nvidia $NVDA's Nov. 12, 2026, press release does not mention a Form 8-K. Jensen Huang's exit as president, CEO and board member, and Colette Kress's appointment as interim CEO, are the kinds of events Item 5.02 is written to cover. Any related filing would appear on EDGAR under Nvidia's company listing.
How companies keep customers and roadmaps steady
Illustration: Quartz
A company keeps customers and product plans steady after a CEO exit by doing three things quickly. It says that operations will continue, names who is in charge and contacts key partners directly.
Nvidia $NVDA's Nov. 12, 2026, announcement of Jensen Huang's departure carried that kind of continuity message. In the statement, Harvey C. Jones said Nvidia expects its operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption. He said interim CEO Colette Kress has a deep understanding of the business, customers, operations and financial position. He also said the board has full confidence in Kress and the leadership team.
Kress, who also remains Nvidia's chief financial officer, addressed the company's outside audiences in her own remarks. She said she is committed to building on the foundation Huang created over the last 33 years. She said Nvidia's focus remains on customers, partners, developers and shareholders.
Each of those four groups has a different stake in a leadership change. Customers want to know that orders, delivery schedules and support agreements will hold. Partners want assurance that joint projects keep moving. Developers who build on a company's platforms look for signs that tools and software will keep getting support. Shareholders want to know who is accountable for results.
The legal structure of a corporation does much of the work. Supply agreements, customer contracts and licensing deals are made in the company's name, not the chief executive's. A CEO's departure does not, on its own, end those obligations.
Product work at a large technology company is spread across many people. Chip designs, software releases and manufacturing plans are run by engineering and operations teams, often on schedules set well in advance. An interim or permanent successor inherits those plans and can decide later whether to change them.
The outreach steps often run at the same time. Senior sales and account executives call major customers to repeat the company's message. Internal memos tell employees who they report to and what stays the same. Investor relations teams take questions from analysts and large shareholders.
Keeping the rest of the executive team in place is part of the same effort. Jones credited Nvidia's leadership team with being instrumental in executing the company's strategy. Public backing of the remaining executives signals support for the people who run daily operations.
The test comes in the months after the change. Customers and investors then see whether shipments, product launches and public commitments arrive as the company said they would.
Why Nvidia's Nov. 17 earnings call matters
Illustration: Quartz
Nvidia $NVDA said it will still release its third-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Tuesday, Nov. 17, as scheduled, despite Jensen Huang's departure. The call puts the company's leadership in front of analysts five days after the board announced the change.
The company said the results are due at about 1:20 p.m. PT. Its earnings call is set to begin at 2 p.m. PT. Keeping the original date means Nvidia's reporting calendar has not shifted along with its management.
Earnings calls at U.S. public companies follow a familiar pattern. Executives walk through revenue, profit and margins for the quarter. They then take questions from Wall Street analysts. Many companies also give a forecast for the quarter ahead.
The Securities and Exchange Commission's Regulation FD bars a public company from giving material information to select investors before releasing it to everyone. A webcast earnings call open to the public is one common way companies meet that rule. Any new detail executives share about the transition on such a call reaches all investors at once.
Colette Kress's dual role changes who answers which questions on this call. Nvidia named her interim CEO while she keeps her job as executive vice president and chief financial officer. CFOs typically present the financial detail on earnings calls. At Nvidia, the person who holds the finance job is now also the company's top executive. Analysts can direct questions about the quarter's numbers and about the leadership change to the same person.
Nvidia's fiscal year does not line up with the calendar year. That is why results released in November 2026 carry a fiscal 2027 label. The figures cover a quarter that closed before the board announced Huang's exit.
The forward-looking parts of the call are the ones most closely tied to the transition. Those include any outlook for the next quarter, any comment on the product roadmap and any update on the board's search for a permanent CEO. Nvidia has not said whether the call will address the search.
The stock had already moved before the call. A Yahoo Finance market widget showed Nvidia shares at 152.96, down 20.77, or 11.96%, when the page was captured. That reading was an intraday snapshot, not a closing price or a final measure of the market's response.

sources.news_title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Ousted Amid Chinese Espionage Concerns and Allegations of Multiple Affairs
sources.text:
By yourNEWS Media Newsroom
Nvidia announced Thursday, Nov. 12, that longtime CEO Jensen Huang has resigned from the company he co-founded in 1993, ending more than three decades of leadership amid an escalating controversy involving national security concerns and allegations of extramarital relationships.
The company confirmed Huang’s immediate departure as president, chief executive officer and a member of its board of directors. Nvidia appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO and named longtime director Harvey C. Jones as its first chairman.
The leadership change came just four days after Nvidia’s board publicly expressed confidence in Huang while announcing an independent investigation into reports that he had maintained a relationship with a woman suspected by U.S. intelligence officials of working for the Chinese government.
According to The Associated Press, Huang faced mounting pressure following reports of an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based technology company Megaspeed International. The two are not related.
U.S. intelligence officials reportedly identified Alice Huang as a potential Chinese intelligence asset amid broader concerns about Beijing’s efforts to obtain restricted American artificial intelligence technology.
The allegations raised questions about whether sensitive corporate information or U.S. national security interests could have been compromised through the relationship. Nvidia has maintained that it has no evidence demonstrating such a breach.
The controversy intensified Wednesday when The New York Times reported that Huang had also engaged in an extramarital relationship with an Nvidia executive who reported directly to him. The additional allegation heightened concerns about corporate governance and potential conflicts of interest.
The Associated Press said it could not independently verify the reported relationships.
Huang had previously acknowledged marital infidelity in a Nov. 8 message to Nvidia employees, apologizing to his family and colleagues.
“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang wrote. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”
He also addressed the security allegations, pledging cooperation with the company’s independent investigation and emphasizing his commitment to protecting American interests.
“I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American,” Huang wrote.
On Nov. 8, Nvidia’s board announced that independent directors would investigate allegations that Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.
“The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders,” the company said in its initial statement.
“While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board’s inquiry will examine all available information.”
The directors concluded that announcement by stating they had confidence in Huang and his leadership team.
Two days later, Nvidia disclosed that the independent directors had retained former acting U.S. Attorney Joon H. Kim and the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct the investigation.
The inquiry comes amid a separate federal investigation involving Megaspeed International and allegations that advanced Nvidia chips subject to U.S. export restrictions may have been transferred to China.
The FBI is investigating the national security allegations, while Singaporean authorities have also examined claims concerning potentially illicit shipments of advanced semiconductors.
Megaspeed has denied evidence of unlawful chip exports and said Thursday that it was cooperating with American authorities. The company also announced that it had retained a U.S. law firm to review its semiconductor inventory and compliance with export regulations.
China has denied allegations that it orchestrated an intelligence operation targeting Huang.
The revelations have intensified scrutiny of Huang’s relationship with President Donald Trump and his longstanding advocacy for allowing Nvidia to sell advanced artificial intelligence processors to Chinese customers.
Huang has argued that permitting American companies to compete in the Chinese market supports U.S. technological leadership, while supporters of tighter export controls contend that advanced AI chips could strengthen China’s military and intelligence capabilities.
Nvidia’s leadership crisis has also unsettled investors. Shares dropped more than 8% in extended trading Wednesday following reports that directors were considering Huang’s removal, and the stock declined approximately 10% in premarket trading Thursday.
The company has lost hundreds of billions of dollars in market capitalization since the controversy emerged, raising concerns about the impact of an abrupt leadership transition at one of the world’s most valuable technology companies.
Kress, who joined Nvidia in September 2013, will continue serving as chief financial officer while assuming the responsibilities of interim CEO. The company said its board would consider both internal and external candidates for a permanent successor.
Jones, an entrepreneur and former executive chairman of Synopsys, expressed confidence in the company’s management team.
“Colette has helped lead NVIDIA through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position,” Jones said.
“The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.”
Kress also pledged continuity following Huang’s departure.
“NVIDIA’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” she said.
Nvidia became a dominant supplier of processors powering advanced artificial intelligence systems under Huang’s leadership, placing the company at the center of the global AI infrastructure expansion.
Its technology supports major cloud computing providers, AI developers and government research operations, making the company’s leadership and security practices significant to both investors and policymakers.
Nvidia is scheduled to release its third-quarter fiscal 2027 financial results Nov. 17, providing investors with an opportunity to assess the company’s financial outlook following the leadership change.
Although Nvidia has confirmed Huang’s resignation, it has not publicly established that he disclosed confidential information or that the alleged foreign intelligence operation successfully compromised company technology.
The independent investigation remains underway as Nvidia begins searching for a permanent chief executive to succeed the founder who led the semiconductor company for 33 years.

Jensen Huang, the founder who propelled Nvidia to become one of the world’s most valuable companies, has resigned from his role as chief executive after 33 years.
The announcement from Nvidia’s board Friday morning ends a whirlwind several days of speculation about Huang’s future in the wake of a stunning corporate scandal.
It came days after the board said it would investigate whether Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort amid reports of his relationship with a woman US officials believe is a Chinese spy, and hours after The New York Times reported that the CEO also had an affair with an executive who reports to him.

The exit marks a sharp fall from grace for Huang, who is largely responsible for kicking off the AI boom. The chips made by the company he founded in 1993 have become critical to the AI infrastructure, putting Nvidia at the center of the AI buildout and thrusting Huang into President Donald Trump’s inner circle.
Colette Kress, current Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of Nvidia, has agreed to serve as Interim Chief Executive Officer, the company said.
Nvidia’s stocks slide
Nvidia’s stock slid about seven per cent in early Frankfurt trading on Thursday after the Wall Street Journal first reported that the company was preparing to fire Huang.
If those losses hold, Nvidia will have lost about $US600 billion ($A878 billion) in market value since the board announced its investigation into his relationship with a businesswoman called Alice Huang, who US officials allege is a Chinese spy.
Revelations that US intelligence was probing Alice Huang for facilitating shipments of Nvidia chips to Chinese firms set off a series of events.
Wall Street began raising questions about Nvidia’s governance and Jensen Huang’s personal conduct while the company’s board launched an internal investigation and hired outside counsel.
US politicians also began to push for tighter curbs on chip exports to China.
Chinese authorities have denied the allegations.
Alice Huang is currently living in Beijing with the knowledge of security officials, Bloomberg News reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
Chinese foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said in Beijing on Thursday that the US should stop making up “so-called spy stories” to justify technology blockades
The leadership upheaval comes just days before investors are set to hear from Nvidia on its financial performance and outlook, with its quarterly results due on November 17.
Earlier on Wednesday, the New York Times reported that Huang had also had an extramarital affair with a company executive who reported to him.
The relationship was with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, the New York Times said, citing five people who worked at the company.
When reached by phone on Wednesday and asked about his relationship with Powell, Huang said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly.”
He then hung up, the New York Times reported.
Investors and analysts said that while demand for Nvidia’s chips would be unlikely to drop in the near term, the broader universe of companies backed by Nvidia - largely customers building data centres that will use its chips - might suffer.
“They are financing their customers. In these types of booms or bubbles, sometimes all it takes is a slowdown to shift it into the bust phase,” said Nick Ferres, chief investment officer at Vantage Point Asset Management in Singapore.
