A memo circulated by US intelligence this past spring alleged Alice Huang was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security.
She was among the attendees at a dinner hosted by Jensen Huang at a Chinese restaurant in Taipei on May 22, 2025, during Computex, the island’s top tech expo.
At one point, Jensen Huang can be seen putting his arm around Alice Huang as she kisses him on the right cheek, press livestreams show. She visited Taiwan a total of eight times in 2024 and 2025, a Taiwanese government minister said Thursday.
Meanwhile, Megaspeed International has also announced the probe after Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s CEO, admitted to having an affair, reportedly with a former Megaspeed executive who the United States suspects of being a Chinese intelligence asset.
Quick Answers
Jensen Huang resigned from his position as Nvidia's CEO and board member following his admission to an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, a woman accused by U.S. intelligence of acting as a Chinese spy. The Nvidia board had previously initiated an independent probe into the reporting that he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

sources.news_title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after his affair raises national security concerns
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns Amid Scandal Involving Alleged Chinese Spy, CFO To Take Over
sources.text:
Nvidia has been thrown into turmoil after co-founder and chief executive Jensen Huang stepped down following a series of damaging reports involving two alleged extramarital affairs, one of which reportedly involved a Chinese businesswoman suspected by US authorities of having links to Beijing’s intelligence network.
The unexpected departure marks a major turning point for the American technology giant, which has become one of the world’s most influential companies amid the explosive growth of artificial intelligence (AI).
Huang, 63, will also leave Nvidia’s board of directors, ending his more than three-decade association with the company he helped establish.
The company confirmed that chief financial officer Colette Kress would assume the role of interim chief executive while the board searches for a permanent replacement. Both internal and external candidates are being considered.
Scandal Puts Nvidia Under Intense Scrutiny
Huang’s resignation comes after reports emerged about his alleged relationships with two women, including a Chinese businesswoman identified as Alice Huang.
US authorities reportedly suspect Alice Huang of having connections to Chinese intelligence, although Beijing has denied allegations that she was acting as a spy.
The controversy has attracted considerable attention because of Alice Huang’s reported association with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that was described as an official Nvidia cloud partner with priority access to its advanced chips.
Washington has also reportedly been investigating whether Megaspeed was involved in helping China obtain restricted artificial intelligence chips in breach of US export controls.
Separately, The New York Times reported that Huang had also been involved in an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, an Nvidia vice-president overseeing its healthcare business who reportedly reported directly to him.
Nvidia had previously launched an internal investigation, led by independent directors and supported by external legal advisers, into whether Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.
Singapore Connection Adds Another Dimension
The controversy has also drawn attention to Singapore because of the investigations surrounding Megaspeed and Alice Huang.
Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs previously confirmed that local police were investigating Super Micro as part of a wider probe involving Megaspeed and Alice Huang.
Authorities had also contacted the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and the US Department of Justice for assistance. However, the ministry said Singapore had received limited information and assistance from the American agencies.
In a separate development, Singapore authorities said Alice Huang had been barred from re-entering the country, citing insufficient evidence that she had committed offences in connection with the Megaspeed investigation.
Meanwhile, Bloomberg News reported that the US Department of Justice was investigating Alice Huang over whether entities linked to her were involved in attempts to smuggle Super Micro Computer products into China.
The investigation is particularly significant given Washington’s restrictions on exporting advanced semiconductor technology to China, an increasingly sensitive issue amid the ongoing competition between the two countries over artificial intelligence.
Nvidia Faces Uncertainty Over Its Next Leader
Huang’s departure raises questions about the future direction of Nvidia, which has become a central player in the global AI industry.
Under his leadership, the company’s graphics processing units (GPUs) evolved from products primarily associated with gaming into essential hardware for training and operating advanced AI systems.
The company’s growing influence helped push its market valuation to almost US$6 trillion at one point, making it the world’s most valuable publicly listed company.
Huang also developed a reputation as one of the technology industry’s most recognisable executives, frequently appearing at major technology conferences in his trademark leather jacket.
With Kress now serving as interim CEO, attention is turning towards potential successors.
Longtime Nvidia engineer Ian Buck has also emerged as a possible candidate. Buck played an important role in developing CUDA, Nvidia’s software platform that has become a major competitive advantage in the AI computing market.
Analysts believe the company’s biggest immediate challenge may not be its technology roadmap, but maintaining the coordination and execution that Huang had overseen for decades.
US Political Fallout Could Follow
The controversy could extend beyond Nvidia and potentially affect US technology export policy.
Huang had previously advocated maintaining access to the Chinese market, arguing for a less restrictive approach towards selling certain Nvidia products to Chinese customers.
His position reportedly aligned with US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who has also faced questions over the administration’s handling of semiconductor exports to China.
Reuters reported that senior White House officials were discussing whether Lutnick should be removed from his position amid the growing controversy.
US President Donald Trump had previously praised Huang’s contributions to the country, saying that the Nvidia chief had told him he was unaware of Alice Huang’s alleged intelligence connections.
Trump also reportedly suggested former Apple chief executive Tim Cook as a possible replacement for Huang.
Nvidia shares fell approximately 4.8 per cent following news of the resignation, although rival chipmakers AMD and Broadcom recorded gains of around 6 per cent each.
For Nvidia, the immediate priority will be ensuring a smooth leadership transition while protecting its position in an increasingly competitive global AI market.
The departure of its co-founder leaves the company facing one of the most consequential leadership changes in its history, with potential implications extending from Silicon Valley to Singapore and the wider US-China technology rivalry.

sources.news_title: Jensen Huang Resigns; Nvidia Reverses Board Structure, Appoints Interim CEO
sources.text:
Six months after defending its decision to operate without a board chair, Nvidia has abandoned that arrangement, installing its first chair and handing executive control to its chief financial officer following the immediate resignation of co-founder Jensen Huang.
The leadership overhaul comes five days before Nvidia is scheduled to report quarterly financial results, with the company previously forecasting $108.0 billion in revenue. The changes also follow an independent investigation into reports that Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.
Nvidia appointed longtime director Harvey C. Jones as its first board chair and named CFO Colette Kress interim chief executive. Kress will retain her finance responsibilities while the board searches for a permanent successor, considering both internal and external candidates.
Huang also resigned from the board, ending his 33-year tenure leading the company he co-founded in 1993.
Board structure reversed
The appointments mark a departure from the governance framework Nvidia described in its May 12 proxy statement.
At the time, the board defended its arrangement of having an independent lead director rather than a chair, arguing that the structure ensured each director had an equal voice in management oversight.
Nvidia said the arrangement promoted independent supervision, distributed responsibilities between executives and directors, and provided adequate oversight without appointing a chairperson.
Stephen C. Neal served as lead independent director under that structure.
Jones, who joined Nvidia’s board in 1993, has experience in semiconductor design software and previously served as chief executive and executive chairman of Synopsys. Nvidia’s 2026 proxy listed him as a member of its audit and nominating and corporate governance committees.
The company’s announcement did not explain why the board abandoned its previous structure or how Jones’ appointment would affect the existing lead-director position.
The change separates formal board leadership from executive management at the same time that Nvidia has temporarily consolidated its chief executive and finance responsibilities under Kress.
Kress joined Nvidia in September 2013 after holding finance positions at Microsoft and Cisco. Her appointment puts an executive responsible for Nvidia’s financial reporting, capital allocation, and investor communications in charge of its broader operations.
A $108 billion quarter without Huang
Nvidia’s leadership transition follows a period of extraordinary financial expansion. The company reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $96.2 billion, an increase of 106% year over year and 18% sequentially.
Data center revenue reached $89.0 billion, up 117% from the previous year. Operating income rose 124% to $63.7 billion, while net income increased 126% to $59.7 billion.
For the third quarter, Nvidia projected revenue of $108.0 billion, plus or minus 2%, alongside a gross margin of approximately 74%.
The guidance did not assume any data center compute revenue from China.
Nvidia also reported approximately $99.0 billion remaining under its share repurchase authorization at the end of the second quarter, after returning about $26.0 billion to shareholders through repurchases and dividends during the period.
These figures establish the financial scale of the business Kress is assuming, including responsibility for managing Nvidia’s growth, expenditures, shareholder returns, and relationships with major AI infrastructure customers.
The company has retained its November 17 earnings schedule, with financial results expected at approximately 1:20 p.m. Pacific Time and a conference call at 2 p.m.
Leadership crisis investigation
Huang’s departure follows several days of scrutiny surrounding his personal relationships and potential national-security exposure.
On November 8, Nvidia’s board announced an independent investigation after reports alleged that Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.
The company said at the time that it had no reason to believe national security or Nvidia’s proprietary information had been compromised.
Huang separately acknowledged in a message to employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife. He also pledged to cooperate with the board’s investigation.
On November 10, Nvidia announced that its independent directors had retained former acting US Attorney Joon H. Kim and Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct the inquiry.
According to Reuters, reporting about Huang’s relationship with a businesswoman suspected by US authorities of having Chinese intelligence connections intensified scrutiny of the CEO. Beijing has denied the espionage allegation.
The New York Times also reported a separate relationship involving a senior Nvidia executive who reported to Huang.
Meanwhile, Nvidia’s directors were reportedly preparing to remove Huang. The company’s eventual announcement characterized his departure as a resignation and did not identify a formal cause.
Nvidia has not publicly disclosed findings establishing that Huang compromised company information, violated export controls, or knowingly participated in an intelligence operation.
The company’s shares fell more than 12% in early trading on Thursday, according to Reuters, putting the chipmaker on course to lose approximately $500 billion in market capitalization at that point in the session.
In its leadership announcement, the board said it expected operations, customer commitments, and the company’s product roadmap to continue without interruption.
Jones cited Kress’ experience managing Nvidia’s financial organization and working with its customers and operating teams as grounds for the board’s confidence in the interim appointment.
Kress committed to maintaining Nvidia’s existing business priorities and executing its technology strategy.

sources.news_title: Jensen Huang steps down as Nvidia CEO after 33 years amid reports that prompted investigation
sources.text:
After 33 years at the helm of Nvidia, co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang has resigned. During that time, the company became one of the most important names in the global technology industry.
The board confirmed the news on Thursday and said Huang’s departure takes effect immediately. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will lead the company on an interim basis until a permanent successor is chosen, while continuing in her current role.
Të lidhura
None found
The resignation follows a turbulent period for Nvidia, marked by media reports alleging that Huang had two extramarital relationships. According to those reports, one involved Alice Huang, whom U.S. authorities suspect may have ties to Chinese intelligence services.
Another report alleged that Huang had a relationship with an Nvidia employee who reported directly to him. The board had previously announced an independent investigation, overseen by a committee of independent directors and assisted by an outside law firm.
In a November 8 statement, the board said it had no reason to believe that company secrets or U.S. national security had been compromised. It stressed, however, that the investigation would examine all available information.
Financial markets reacted immediately to Huang’s departure. Nvidia shares fell sharply in both premarket trading and Thursday’s session, as investors expressed concern about the company’s future without the leader who had guided it for more than three decades.
Nvidia ranks among the most influential companies in U.S. stock markets and plays a key role in the development of artificial intelligence. Its graphics processors and data-center chips have been among the main drivers of the global boom in the field. For that reason, the change in the company’s leadership matters to the technology sector, financial markets and the strategic interests of the United States.
U.S. House Speaker Mike Johnson described the resignation as a major and unexpected development. He said Nvidia is important not only to the U.S. economy but also to national security, and that the matter is being followed with great interest and attention.
Johnson said he had learned of the departure only minutes earlier, as he headed toward the House chamber. According to him, some members of Congress want to question Huang, and that will happen if the House decides to do so.
The House speaker added that many facts remain to be clarified, so he is reserving personal judgment. Nevertheless, he said that, on a personal level, Huang appears to have done what was right for the company and the country.
Huang’s departure closes an era for Nvidia. He co-founded the company in 1993 and led its transition from making chips for video games to becoming one of the leading forces in the artificial intelligence revolution.

Equity index futures fell overnight as reports that Nvidia’s Jensen Huang was stepping down unsettled the AI sector. Thursday’s results from Applied Materials, Cisco and Nebius will provide additional tests of the AI spending cycle, while Friday’s PPI report will help determine whether inflation concerns continue to offset improving corporate sentiment.
CURRENCIES

The dollar’s strong move upwards as of recent reflects economic data that has shifted the debate from whether the Fed raises rates in December toward how much further rates will move in 2027. New York Fed President John Williams’ comments later Thursday will be closely watched for indications of whether support is broadening for a larger increase or a faster sequence of quarter-point hikes. Many banks expect another BOJ hike in December, but the prospect of continued Fed tightening remains a counterweight to yen support.

The combination of softer Australian activity indicators and expectations for further US tightening continues to offer downside pressures. Markets expect that Australian rates have peaked, with a quarter-point cut fully priced by the end of 2027.

sources.news_title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO, Colette Kress steps in
sources.text:
Jensen Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has run it ever since, resigned as the company’s CEO on 12 November 2026, effective immediately. Nvidia’s chief financial officer, Colette Kress, will run the company as interim CEO while the board looks for a permanent replacement.
The short version
- Huang stepped down as Nvidia’s president, CEO and board member, effective immediately, according to Nvidia’s announcement.
- CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and keeps her finance job until a permanent CEO is named. The board says it will look at internal and outside candidates.
- Harvey C. Jones, a Nvidia board member and former CEO of chip design software maker Synopsys, becomes the company’s first board chair.
- Nvidia still plans to report its quarterly results on 17 November.
Why he left
Nvidia’s announcement does not give a reason. It came after two days of reports about two relationships Huang had. On 11 November, The Information reported that he had an affair with a woman U.S. reports link to a network accused of moving Nvidia chips to China. China denies she is a spy, and the claims against her have not been proven. That evening, The New York Times reported a second affair, with a senior Nvidia employee who reported to him. Neither Huang nor Nvidia has confirmed that report. The Wall Street Journal then reported that the board was meeting to decide whether to remove him.
In a memo to employees reported by several outlets, Huang admitted to the first affair and said he was “deeply sorry.”
The board said it has “full confidence in Colette and the leadership team.” Kress joined Nvidia in 2013 after nearly 25 years in finance jobs at Cisco and Microsoft.
What changes for you: if you use Nvidia products, such as a GeForce graphics card, its drivers or the GeForce Now game streaming service, Nvidia has not announced any change to them. If you own Nvidia shares, directly or through an index fund that holds big US tech companies, expect a bumpy few days. Nvidia’s shares fell sharply before the market opened on 12 November. TechCity is not a financial adviser.
What happens next
The next date to watch is Tuesday, 17 November. Nvidia reports its results for the August to October quarter at about 1:20 p.m. Pacific time, with a call for investors at 2 p.m. It will be Kress’s first time on that call as interim CEO.
What we don’t know yet
- Whether Huang chose to leave or the board asked him to go.
- Who the permanent CEO will be, and how long the search will take.
- Whether any government inquiry into the China report goes further, and what it could mean for Nvidia’s chip sales.
We’ll update this story as Nvidia says more.
